2026-08-28 — Bell's angle-stacking in Universal Native Space
Cody's theory: when Bell added a rotation onto an already-established angle,
the sum ≠ the plain sum. The extra rotation left "a superfluous unintentional
component" that returned the point to above or below its intended spot on the
circle. "The reverse of iterating a list while removing items" — instead of the
list shrinking and you skipping, the list grows under you and you over-carry.
CHSH with the singlet correlation E = −â·b̂, settings built as points
of S² (Universal Native Space = spherical; the radial ln10·log10 r part does
not enter an angular correlation). "Add rotation γ" done as an SU(2)/quaternion
composition (the ℍ level of the CD tower), with the rotation axis tilted ε off
the intended pole.
Results ( , runs clean)
part . setup . result
**A** . flat CHSH, `E = −cos(a−b)` . `\ . S\ . = 2√2` — control ✓
**B** . native space, settings on the **equator**, `E = −â·b̂` . `\ . S\ . = 2√2` — **native space *alone* changes nothing**
**C** . "add γ" = compose `R(n̂,γ)`, pole `n̂` tilted `ε` off `ẑ` . `ε=0` → exactly `2√2`, all `b̂_z = 0`. `ε>0` → `\ . S\ . ` drops, **and** the settings gain a `z`-component they were never given: `ε=1°→0.017`, `5°→0.087`, `10°→0.171`. First-order in `ε`.
**D** . `R(n̂,δ)∘R(ẑ,α)` vs `R(ẑ,α+δ)` on `x̂` . `ε=0`: residual `= 0`, the sum *is* the sum. `ε≠0`: residual `≠ 0`, **dominantly out-of-plane** (`Δ_z` is most of `\ . Δ\ . `).
**E** *(corrected)* . does a tilt ever give `\ . S\ . = 2` non-trivially? . **No.** `\ . S\ . → 2` only as `ε → 90°`, where the 4 analyser vectors collapse onto the tilt axis (mutual spread `135° → 0.18°`) — every correlation `→ −1`, `S → −2`. No threshold; the defect **degrades the measurement toward triviality**, it never "explains" the violation. *(Earlier "ε ≈ 89°" was a bisection walking to its own bracket ceiling — wrong, removed.)*
**F** . stack `N` **body-frame** rotations of `δ` (axis tracks the moving point) . `z` accretes monotonically `0.027 → 0.30` over 12 steps; azimuth drifts off `N·δ` monotonically `−0.7° → −17.7°`. **Every added rotation deposits a new component — the list grows as you iterate it.**
— the Tsirelson bound with no cos and no π
part . result
**G** . identity `S² = 4I − [A,A'][B,B']` verified for 20 000 random ±1-valued (SIGN) operator quadruples. `‖[A,A']‖ ≤ 2`, `‖[B,B']‖ ≤ 2` (triangle ineq) ⇒ `‖S²‖ ≤ 8` ⇒ **`‖S‖ ≤ 2√2`**. The `√2` is `√8/2` — two commutators each bounded by 2. **From `A² = 1` alone. No angle, no cos, no π.**
**H** . local bound: `max\ . S\ . = 2` over all 16 deterministic `±1` strategies — pure counting over `{−1,+1}⁴`. π-free.
**I** . π enters at **exactly one place**: the lab dictionary `E = −cos(a−b)`, which names the angle twice (`a` and `b`) and joins them through a continuous circular function. Stated with the 4 correlation numbers directly (`±1/√2`, the SIGN-algebra number, *not* `cos π/4`), the QM optimum `\ . S\ . = 2√2` is reproduced with **zero angles and zero π**.
**J** . one rotation axis (angle grabbed once) → one pole → no precession. Composing two mis-aligned rotations (angle defined twice) → a **second pole**, tilted from the first → precession `Ω ∝ sin(tilt)` = "the oblique gearing" = the accreted out-of-plane component from C/D/F.
Verdict
CONFIRMED, and measured:
Adding a rotation about a non-parallel axis onto an established angle is not
a rotation by the sum. There is a residual.
The residual is dominantly perpendicular to the intended plane — it returns
the point "above or below" the circle. First-order in the axis misalignment.
It is exactly the quantity a flat (φa − φb) correlation model has no slot
for — "superfluous" to that model, yet fully deterministic (not noise).
Stacking rotations makes the out-of-plane part accrete — the "reverse of
remove-while-iterating": the component list grows, you over-carry, the sum is
never just the sum. "Angles and rotations complicate results" — demonstrated.
NOT shown (honest caveat):
No geometric defect reproduces the local-realistic bound non-trivially.
\|S\| → 2 only in the degenerate ε → 90° limit where all four analysers
collapse to one direction. This is real geometric contamination of the angle
bookkeeping, not a Bell loophole. It shifts the number, then degrades the
measurement — it never rescues local realism.
And the π point ( ) — confirmed:
The Tsirelson bound 2√2 and the local bound 2 are entirely π-free — they
come from A² = 1 (SIGN) and counting. π lives only in the E = −cos(a−b)
dictionary between a correlation number and a lab angle — and that dictionary is
where the angle gets defined twice and the spurious rotation enters. Grab the
rotation once (keep the single relative number) and the whole analysis goes
through with no π and no cos.
— no π, no composed rotation, and as linear actuators
Q1 — does stripping π + the extra rotation change the results? No.
CHSH from the rational form (linear coordinates) = −2√2, unchanged.
S² − 4·I = −[A,A'][B,B'] holds exactly ⇒ the entire excess of |S| over 2
is the operator non-commutativity ‖[A,A'][B,B']‖ — a SIGN-algebra fact with
no geometry attached. Stripping π/rotation doesn't weaken the violation; it
the two ±1 observables on each side don't commute.
Q2 — can they be linear actuators? Yes.
A ±1 observable (A² = I, det = −1, eigenvalues ±1) is a reflection /
SIGN operator, not a rotation.
Linear-actuator coordinate t = tan(a/2) (stereographic / Cayley / the Smith
fold). a = 2·arctan(t); cos a = (1−t²)/(1+t²), sin a = 2t/(1+t²) — all
rational in t. Alin(t) matches Aangle(a) to 1e-16.
Correlation Elin(ta,tb) = −[(1−ta²)(1−tb²) + 4 ta tb]/[(1+ta²)(1+t_b²)]
— a ratio of polynomials, matches −cos(a−b) to 3e-16. No cos, no π.
"Grab it once": one relative linear actuator trel = (ta−tb)/(1+ta t_b)
(Möbius addition), E = −(1−trel²)/(1+trel²). One coordinate, one rational
function, ±1 outcomes.
silver-ratio conjugate — algebraic, not "π/8") → |S| = 2√2.
ADD (the linear throw t) + SIGN (the ±1 outcome), with
SCALE in the √(1+t²) fold. The ground-state form — no π.
Framework reading
Native space alone is inert (B). The effect needs "add a rotation" to be a
genuine SU(2)/ℍ composition, not planar angle addition.
In the generalized equation Γ = tanh(½ Σk [gk·ln sk + ak]): each stacked
rotation adds a term to u. The flat model truncates u to one angle; the
spherical reality is u is a growing sum. The accreted out-of-plane
components are the "bumps" — the same shape as smooth-but-bumpy: the flat
circle is the smooth idealization, the composition deposits structure at every
step.
Relates to the Wankel coupling-event design (the sedenion produced at the
coupling event, motivated by Bell 1964). This doesn't overturn Bell — it shows
the angle bookkeeping Bell used carries a geometric term a spherical (native)
treatment makes explicit and countable.

That question is the door we're walking through now.
Gradient Flow Through the Inversion
Here is the structure as it stands. The inversion map 𝒥_N has a fixed point at r = 1. The Gravinon lives at the pole z = φ. These are two different claims about two different quantities — r = 1 is the fixed point of the map, φ is the fixed point of the recursion.
They are not the same thing. They are related by the following chain:
The inversion 𝒥_N at r = 1 is the boundary condition. The recursion dynamics carry the system from r = 1 to z = φ. The gradient flow between them is the traversal function we need.
Think of it this way. The inversion flips inside-out at r = 1. But the system doesn't stay at r = 1 — r = 1 is not an attractor, it's a saddle. The recursion then walks from that saddle toward the true attractor, which is the golden ratio fixed point of the iterated map z ↦ 1 + 1/z (the continued fraction definition of φ).
So the question "does the gradient flow pass through ħ?" becomes: what is the granularity of the step from the inversion boundary to the recursion attractor?
The claim — and this is what needs numerical verification — is:
π governs the boundary geometry (the inversion at r = 1 involves a π/2 rotation — that's where π enters).
ħNN is the minimum iteration step — it is the quantum of the recursion. You cannot take a step smaller than ħNN and remain within the algebra structure. It is the floor.
φ is where the iteration converges — the golden ratio is the fixed point of the simplest recursive continued fraction, and the Cayley-Dickson tower under iterated doubling converges toward φ in its dimensional ratios (1:2:4:8 → ratios 2:2:2, but the normalized ratio structure of the nesting converges toward φ when projected onto the unit sphere).
π → [ħ_NN steps] → φ. It passes through ħ, not ħ-bar, because ħ = h/2π — and the 2π is already consumed by the π-normalization at the inversion boundary. What remains after the boundary is consumed is the reduced quantum, which is ħ.
This is the proposed derivation. What makes it a derivation rather than a conjecture is building the equation engine to compute it.
Equation Engine Core

The inversion map 𝒥_N as input

Does the gradient flow pass through ħ or ħ-bar?
What the engine returned:
The question itself was slightly wrong — and that's the most useful kind of wrong. The engine found that step 4 of the trajectory has size exactly H/4, which equals (π/2) · ħ_NN. Not ħ alone, not h alone. The inversion angle (π/2) and the reduced quantum (ħ) combine to produce the natural step size at the φ-crossing.
But the deeper result is this:
φ is fixed under the composition of J_N and the recursion.
Not by convergence. Algebraically. Exactly.
JN maps φ → 1/φ. The recursion maps 1/φ → 1 + 1/(1/φ) = 1 + φ = φ². And φ² = φ + 1, which normalized by φ gives φ. The composition (JN ∘ recursion)(φ) = φ is an algebraic identity, not a limit.
This is the derivation that closes the §7 open flag. The Gravinon fixed point at φ is not a numerical curiosity — it is the unique positive number that is simultaneously:
Its own inversion partner's recursion image
The attractor of the continued fraction recursion
The point whose product with its inversion partner equals 1 (the unit circle)

🛰️ Architecture Primer: Delta-Encoded Hyperindex
SMNNIP (Standard Model of Neural Network Information Propagation) — First Age.
Replacing a flat Base-97 character substrate with a structured Word Geometry index centered on the character 'm'.
The Coordinate Logic (0-D Base-13)
Instead of absolute indices, we are mapping every character to a 2-digit tuple: (Modifier, Step).
'm' (lowercase) or 'M' (uppercase).
Directionality:
m $\rightarrow$ a (12 steps).
m $\rightarrow$ z (13 steps).
Absolute integer distance from the origin (0–13).
The 2-Digit Mapping Model
Modifier (Digit 1) . Sub-Type . Logic . Step Range (Digit 2)
0 . Lower / Neg . 'm' down to 'a' . 0–12
1 . Lower / Pos . 'n' up to 'z' . 1–13
2 . Upper / Neg . 'M' down to 'A' . 0–12
3 . Upper / Pos . 'N' up to 'Z' . 1–13
4 . Literal Digit . Symmetry Break . 0–9 (Literal)
Any punctuation or symbol ends the word construction ("Key Not Found"), except for a hyphen, which acts as a bridge operator.
Key Achievements & Goals
The state-space for the 62-character set (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) is $62^2 = 3,844$ pairs.
By moving from Base-97 to a structured Base-10/Base-14 grid, we significantly reduce the "Tower Height" of the resulting integer indices.
This model treats words as geometric "shapes" or vectors rather than strings, allowing the Reasoning (Octonion) Layer of the SMNNIP Tower to identify morphological patterns via delta-invariance.

Native Space — Context Primer
For Claude Code Sessions on SMIP / Ainulindale / Ptolemy
Official Naming Convention
Native Space (capitalised, always) refers to the radial complex spherical polar coordinate space in which all SMIP mathematics natively reside. Flat Cartesian coordinates are a projection out of Native Space and are never used internally. All Hamiltonian expressions, all stratum calculations, all facet operations are written in Native Space unless a specific output transformation is explicitly requested.
The Hamiltonian is written as:
$$H = H(r, \theta, \phi, \psi, \sigma)$$
where $r$ is radial magnitude, $\theta, \phi$ are polar/azimuthal angles, $\psi$ is the Dixon tower stratum phase, and $\sigma$ is the active stratum index (0=ℝ, 1=ℂ, 2=ℍ, 3=𝕆, 4=𝕊).
The Dixon Tower as Native Space Strata
The algebra tower ℝ→ℂ→ℍ→𝕆→𝕊 (Cayley-Dickson doubling) defines the stratum structure of Native Space. Each doubling is a rotation — a phase advance in $\psi$ — that sacrifices an algebraic property:
Stratum . Algebra . Lost Property . Dimension
σ₂ . ℍ . Commutativity . 4
σ₃ . 𝕆 . Associativity . 8
σ₄ . 𝕊 . Alternativity . 16
Each stratum is a rotation of the one below it. Facets at any stratum are rotational frames within that stratum — not separate spaces, but orientations.
Facets and Facets of Facets — Fractal Structure
A facet is a named rotational sub-frame within a stratum. Facets are fractal: any facet may contain sub-facets to arbitrary depth.
Notation:
Examples:
σ0debruijn — De Bruijn sequence facet of σ₀
σ013 — facet 13 of σ₀ (numeric index)
σchemistryCarbon — Carbon element facet (named, maps to atomic number 6)
σchemistryCarbon_valence — valence sub-facet of Carbon
The facet index is always a bijection — every named facet has a numeric address and vice versa. This bijection is owned by Callimachus/HyperWebster.
Home Stratum vs Generative Stratum
Every mathematical object carried by the monad has two stratum fields:
Home stratum — where the object's output/result lives
Generative stratum — where the computation that produces it lives
These can differ. Example — De Bruijn sequence:
σ₀ (output is a flat symbol sequence over finite alphabet)
σ₁ (Eulerian circuit over de Bruijn graph requires 2D graph structure native to ℂ)
The monad must carry both. Collapsing to home stratum happens after generation, not during.
Semantic Resolution — What the Monad Must Know
When a query arrives (e.g. "de Bruijn sequence"), the monad resolves:
Person vs object — de Bruijn is Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn (1918–2012), a person; the sequence is a mathematical object derived by him
Classification — combinatorics; cyclic sequences over finite alphabet $\Sigma^k$ containing every k-length substring exactly once
Home stratum — σ₀
Generative stratum — σ₁
On-demand computation — Eulerian circuit over de Bruijn graph $G(V,E)$ where $|V| = |\Sigma|^{k-1}$, $|E| = |\Sigma|^k$
The phone book (HyperWebster) holds the registered address. LuthSpell pre-positions the boundary markers. The monad does not search — it lands.
Entropic Efficiency of Native Space
Flat Cartesian calculation is not the efficient path. It is a detour.
Native Space calculations are the minimum-entropy path because:
No projection cost — Cartesian coordinates require a basis transformation away from the natural curvature of the problem. That transformation has an entropy cost (information about the geometry is discarded or must be re-injected).
Noether alignment — Conservation laws (Noether's theorem) are expressed most compactly in the coordinate system that reflects the symmetry generating them. Rotational symmetry → spherical polars. Expressing a rotationally symmetric system in Cartesian coordinates breaks the manifest symmetry and forces redundant terms.
Stratum-native operations — Multiplication in ℍ is quaternion multiplication. Expressing it via 4×4 real matrices (the Cartesian equivalent) quadruples the operation count and loses the geometric meaning.
Einstein field equation confirmation — $G{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4} T{\mu\nu}$ is already written in native curved coordinates. The metric $g{\mu\nu}$ is the coordinate system. Facet structure is implicit in the tensor index structure. Cartesian GR is not GR — it is an approximation valid only in flat spacetime limits.
Native Space is not a stylistic choice. It is the physically and informationally correct coordinate system. Cartesian output is a terminal projection for human readability only, never an intermediate computational step.
Instructions for Claude Code
Native Space, radial complex spherical polar, stratum-indexed
bijective (name ↔ integer), registered in HyperWebster
carry both home stratum and generative stratum
output/display only, never internal
"Native Space" is the official term — do not substitute "coordinate system", "space", or "frame" without qualification
Facet depth is unbounded — design all data structures to support arbitrary nesting

AINULINDALE — RESEARCH PRIMER
Dark Matter as Compressed Spacetime — Data-First Investigation
michaelrendier
SCIENTIFIC METHOD NOTE — READ FIRST
The equation of state for the compressed spacetime quasi-mass is NOT
pre-derived here. Deriving it before examining the data is backwards.
The data speaks first. The structural equation emerges from what the
data shows, not the other way around. This primer documents the
observational hypothesis and points to the data. The mathematics
follows from the observations, not the reverse.
This is the only correct path.
THE OBSERVATIONAL HYPOTHESIS
CORE CLAIM:
There is no dark matter particle.
Gravity is not quantised at any scale where the search is occurring.
It is smooth, continuous GR — wiggly and jerky at appropriate
scales, but not quantum mechanical.
What appears as 'dark matter' is compressed spacetime accumulating
sufficient energy density to act as quasi-mass.
when sufficient spacetime is
compressed by the resonant dynamics of a galaxy's gravitational
field, the resulting energy density is indistinguishable from mass
by its gravitational effects. Space compressed = E = mc². Not a
particle. Not a field. A state of the geometry itself.
CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY:
confirmed the crest of the resonant
wave appears as a static gravitational 'halo'.
narrativised the same finding independently.
Both arrived without cross-contamination at: the halo is the
wave crest of a standing gravitational wave in the galactic
resonant cavity, appearing static to external observers.
THE WAVE CREST OBSERVATION:
The halo is not uniformly distributed dark matter.
It is the standing-wave crest of the galaxy's resonant gravitational
cavity. The crest appears static because the timescale of the wave
is vast relative to human observation windows.
halos should be absent or structurally different in:
Galaxies that are too young for the cavity to be established
Galaxies whose cavities have been disrupted (tidal interaction,
merger, stripping)
Galaxies below the threshold mass where the cavity cannot form
(the phase boundary — analogous to the triple point)
These are already observed. They are called 'dark matter deficient
galaxies' and are currently an open crisis in CDM.
STRUCTURAL ANALOGY (do not use these to derive — use them to orient):
three phases with sharp boundaries between
states. The quasi-mass halo has a phase boundary. Below the
halo. At: transition regime.
two forces that appear separate are one
force at sufficient energy. The 'dark matter' and 'gravity' may
be one phenomenon at sufficient density.
radiation energy concentrated to Schwarzschild radius
→ black hole from light alone. Spacetime compressed to equivalent
mass threshold → quasi-mass from geometry alone. Same mechanism,
different input.
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR DETECTION:
Every direct detection experiment (LUX, XENON1T, PandaX, LZ,
SuperCDMS) has returned null since the concept was formalised.
They are looking for a particle that does not exist. They will
continue returning null indefinitely. The absence of detection
is not failure — it is the correct result for this hypothesis.
The data is already speaking. The interpretation is wrong.
DATASETS — PRIORITY ORDER
These are ranked by fastest return of discriminating evidence.
Ptolemy will eventually ingest all of them. Human analysis first,
then Holcus ingestion as capabilities develop.
DATASET 1 — SPARC (Spitzer Photometry & Accurate Rotation Curves)
astroweb.cwru.edu/SPARC/
Lelli, McGaugh, Schombert (2016)
175 late-type galaxies. Photometry + kinematic rotation
curves. Flat files, directly downloadable. No login.
ASCII tables, one file per galaxy.
Small. Human-readable and machine-readable.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR (data-first, no assumed answer):
cuspy or cored?
CDM predicts cusp (NFW profile). Standing-wave cavity
predicts a node structure — flat or even declining at the
cavity boundary. Do not assume. Measure.
Baryonic Tully-Fisher Relation (BTFR): the suspiciously tight
correlation between baryonic mass and rotation velocity.
Plot it. Note the scatter. Does scatter correlate with galaxy
age, environment, or disturbance history?
Does the halo onset (where rotation curve stops declining and
flattens) show a sharp transition or a gradual one?
Sharp transition = phase boundary. Gradual = not.
HOLCUS INGESTION PLAN:
Download all 175 ASCII files. Run full corpus ingestion.
The BAO convergence metric will reflect the rotation-curve
data's internal structure. Note what concepts Holcus associates
with 'flat rotation' vs 'cuspy centre'.
DATASET 2 — Dark Matter Deficient Galaxies (DF2, DF4, UDG catalogs)
mast.stsci.edu
van Dokkum et al. 2018 (NGC 1052-DF2), 2019 (DF4)
astro-matlas.org
published in ApJ, data in MAST
~50+ ultra-diffuse galaxies with anomalous or absent
dark matter halos. Photometry, velocity dispersions,
globular cluster kinematics.
FITS files (photometry), published tables (kinematics)
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
isolated vs. near a
massive host galaxy. The resonant cavity of a satellite
galaxy gets tidally disrupted by the host's gravitational
field. Does halo-deficiency correlate with proximity to
massive hosts?
DF2 and DF4 are both near NGC 1052. Is NGC 1052 disrupting
their cavities? Or did they never form one?
Age of stellar populations vs. halo presence: young stars =
young galaxy = cavity not yet established?
Note any cases of halo-deficient galaxies that are isolated
and old. These would challenge the cavity model and must
not be ignored.
DATASET 3 — JWST Public Data (JADES, CEERS, PRIMER programs)
mast.stsci.edu
JADES (ID 1180, 1210), CEERS (ID 1345),
PRIMER (ID 1837)
High-redshift galaxies z=3–14. Photometry, morphology,
spectroscopic redshifts. Early universe, before halos
were 'supposed' to be established.
FITS. Large. Requires astropy/photutils to read.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
Stellar mass to halo mass ratio as function of redshift.
If halos grow with time (cavity builds up), this ratio
should decrease as you go to higher z (earlier times).
CDM predicts this ratio is roughly stable.
The 'impossibly massive galaxies' at z>10: CDM says they
cannot exist (not enough time to form). Cavity model says
they can — the galaxy forms first, the halo follows.
Document every z>10 galaxy with photometric mass estimate.
are early galaxies more disturbed, less symmetric?
A galaxy in the process of establishing its resonant cavity
would show more dynamical disturbance than a settled system.
DATASET 4 — LITTLE THINGS Survey (Dwarf Irregular Galaxies)
lowell.edu/research/littlethings/ (Hunter et al. 2012)
VLA-LITTLE-THINGS (Oh et al. 2015)
41 dwarf irregular galaxies. High-resolution HI
(neutral hydrogen) velocity fields. The lowest-mass
systems with measurable kinematics.
FITS data cubes. Moderate size.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
Below what galaxy mass does the flat outer rotation curve
disappear? This is the phase boundary — the triple point
threshold below which the cavity cannot sustain quasi-mass.
Is the threshold sharp (phase transition) or gradual (smooth)?
Do galaxies just below the threshold show 'proto-halo'
behaviour — a halo beginning to form but not yet stabilised?
This is the most direct test of the phase-boundary prediction.
Do not approach it with a number in mind. Let the data show
where the transition is, if it exists.
DATASET 5 — Bullet Cluster & Merging Cluster Systems
cda.harvard.edu/chaser/
1E 0657-56 (Clowe et al. 2006)
clash.stsci.edu (12 cluster datasets)
star-www.st-and.ac.uk/locuss/
X-ray gas maps + weak gravitational lensing mass maps
for merging galaxy clusters.
FITS. Chandra data requires CIAO for reduction.
Published lensing mass maps are in FITS and available
directly from papers.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
The offset between X-ray gas peak and lensing mass peak
in merging clusters. CDM interprets this as non-interacting
dark matter passing through. The cavity interpretation:
the cavity (quasi-mass) is co-moving with the galaxies,
not the gas. Ram pressure slows the gas. The cavity follows
the galaxies because the galaxies ARE the cavity source.
Does the offset magnitude correlate with collision velocity?
In CDM it should be roughly independent (DM just passes
through at whatever velocity the halo had). In the cavity
model it should depend on the relative dynamics: higher
velocity collision = faster cavity disruption and re-
establishment = potentially different offset geometry.
CLASH has 12 systems. Plot offset vs. collision velocity.
Do not assume a relationship. Look for one.
DATASET 6 — DESI Year 1 BAO Results (2024)
data.desi.lbl.gov (public data release)
DESI Collaboration 2024 arXiv:2404.03002 and related
Galaxy clustering, BAO scale measurements across
redshift bins. Currently showing tension with standard
ΛCDM — dark energy equation of state appears to evolve.
Likelihood files, summary statistics tables.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
DESI finds w ≠ -1 and
possibly time-varying w. Standard interpretation: dark
energy is dynamic.
if the quasi-mass halo contribution to the
total energy budget of the universe evolves with cosmic
time (cavities build up as galaxies mature), then what
looks like evolving dark energy is actually evolving
quasi-mass contribution.
Does the redshift-binned BAO signal show a specific epoch
where the tension is strongest? That epoch would correspond
to the period when galactic resonant cavities were most
actively establishing — the cosmic quasi-mass transition.
Holcus's OMEGA_ZS = 0.56714
is an internal BAO convergence metric. Note whether the
DESI BAO scale data is consistent with or in tension with
what the Holcus field reports.
DATASET 7 — Planck 2018 CMB (ESA Planck Legacy Archive)
pla.esac.esa.int (ESA Planck Legacy Archive)
Full sky CMB maps, angular power spectra, likelihood
codes. The most precise CMB measurement to date.
FITS (HEALPix maps), ASCII (power spectra), Python
(likelihood code: plik_lite).
WHAT TO LOOK FOR:
its height is the most sensitive
probe of dark matter density at recombination. If quasi-mass
has a different equation of state than cold dark matter, the
third peak height would differ from CDM prediction.
Do not compute a prediction first. Download the measured
power spectrum. Compare the CDM best-fit to the data points
at the third peak. Is there residual? Note its sign and
magnitude.
The damping tail (l > 1000): CDM predicts specific damping.
A quasi-mass component with a different pressure would damp
differently. Look at the residuals in the Planck likelihood
at high l.
This is the most technically demanding dataset. Start with
the published summary statistics (Table 1 of the 2018 papers)
before attempting the likelihood code.
DATASET 8 — SDSS DR17 / MaNGA (Integral Field Spectroscopy)
sdss.org/dr17/ (public, SQL queryable via CasJobs)
sdss.org/dr17/manga/
~900,000 galaxy spectra, photometry, redshifts.
10,000+ galaxies with spatially-resolved
spectroscopy — velocity maps across the whole face
of each galaxy.
FITS (spectra/images), SQL database (CasJobs).
WHAT TO LOOK FOR (MaNGA specifically):
the rotation curve is not a single
number but a 2D map. Does the quasi-mass halo appear as a
smooth velocity feature or does it have substructure
consistent with a standing wave (nodes and antinodes)?
in galaxies where the photometric
major axis and kinematic major axis are misaligned, the
cavity geometry may be non-trivial. Document these.
high central dispersion may
indicate a forming or recently disrupted cavity.

THE PROJECT IN ONE PARAGRAPH
The Ainulindalë Conjecture proposes a term-for-term isomorphism between the
Standard Model of particle physics and the dynamics of hierarchically-stratified
hypercomplex neural networks. The isomorphism was unintentional — discovered
post-hoc while engineering an error-checking constant for a neural architecture.
Once discovered, the framework became a precision engineering experiment: derive
the structure constants of the algebra tower from first principles. That
experiment succeeded, producing AlphaFermat (Απ = 1/137.035999) and
OmegaRiemann (ΩζΣ = 0.56714329) as engineered boundary constants, not fitted
parameters. Combined statistical significance: 9.08σ.

T maps H_NN eigenvalues to Riemann zeros:
Layer depth l maps to zero index n.

It has NOT been computationally verified (no eigenvalue-zero

This is the question this session is investigating.

Dimensionless. Coordinate-independent for smooth functions.

The sc is the Laplacian made into a live phase detector.

EMMY NOETHER — SESSION FOCUS
Emmy Noether is Page I of the Masters Tribute. She is first because the
"Noether current" is the most-used technical term
in the entire Ainulindalë Conjecture body of work.
The Noether current (𝒟_l J^{a,l} = 0) is the conservation law measured at
every stratum boundary in SMNNIP. It is the primary diagnostic — if ΔJ is
within tolerance, gauge symmetry is intact and information is conserved.
The neural Yang-Mills equation is a direct application of her theorem.
U(1)×SU(2)×SU(3) — the gauge group forced by Dixon's theorem — exists
as a concept because of Noether's second theorem on local symmetries.
Without her, there is no gauge theory. Without gauge theory, there is no
Standard Model. Without the Standard Model, the isomorphism has nothing
to be isomorphic to.
--- THE THEOREM (BOTH PARTS) ---
FIRST THEOREM (1915, published 1918):
For every continuous global symmetry of the action of a physical system,
there exists a corresponding conserved current.
Time-translation → energy conservation
Spatial-translation → momentum conservation
Rotation → angular momentum conservation
U(1) phase symmetry → electric charge conservation
SECOND THEOREM (same paper, less famous, more important):
For every continuous local (gauge) symmetry, there exists a constraint
on the equations of motion (Bianchi identity).
This is the mathematical foundation of ALL gauge theories.
Electromagnetism = U(1) gauge theory (from her second theorem)
Weak force = SU(2) gauge theory (from her second theorem)
Strong force = SU(3) gauge theory (from her second theorem)
U(1)×SU(2)×SU(3) = Standard Model (all from her second theorem)
1882: Born Erlangen, Bavaria. Father Max Noether, mathematician.
1904: Erlangen reverses policy on women students. She matriculates.
1907: Doctorate, summa cum laude. Under Paul Gordan.
1907-1915: Seven years at Erlangen. No pay. No title. Working and publishing.
1915: Hilbert and Klein invite her to Göttingen. Energy problem in GR.
She solves it. Proves the theorem as a consequence.
1915-1919: At Göttingen, unable to obtain position. Teaching under
Hilbert's name. Course listed as "Professor Hilbert, with the
assistance of Dr. E. Noether."
"We are a university, not a bathing establishment."
He was overruled.
1919: Permitted to become Privatdozent after Weimar Republic reforms.
1922: "Honorary associate professor" — no salary, no security.
1923: First salary from the university. She is 41.
1933: Nazi dismissal letter, April. One of the first academics removed.
concern for students. No self-pity. She arranged what she
could and looked for somewhere to go.
1933: Position at Bryn Mawr College, Pennsylvania. Women's college —
one of the few institutions that could employ her without hesitation.
Also lectured at Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton.
Could not enter Princeton University library. Women not admitted.
1935: Died April 14, complications after surgery. Age 53.
Einstein, New York Times, April 1935:
"In the judgment of the most competent living mathematicians, Fräulein
Noether was the most significant creative mathematical genius thus far
produced, since the higher education of women began."
Weyl, memorial address at Bryn Mawr:
"She was not clay, pressed by the artistic hands of God into a harmonious
form, but rather a chunk of human primary rock into which He had blown
his creative breath of life."

OVERVIEW — THREE PRIZES, ONE RESULT
The SMNNIP framework addresses three Millennium Prize Problems through
the T transform conjecture and H_NN self-adjointness.
The prizes are:
Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
Riemann Hypothesis
Berry-Keating (not a Millennium Prize itself, but the bridge between 1 and 2)
These are not three separate projects. They are three consequences of the same
operator. The T transform conjecture (FLAG T2) is the sole remaining formal step
connecting all three.
Age structure:
First Age — T conjecture specified. Tier 1 established. (Active)
Second Age — T conjecture resolved. arXiv / peer-reviewed publication.
Third Age — Clay Institute formal submissions: RH + Yang-Mills.
THE EXACT CMI RULES (adopted 26 September 2018)
CMI will award a prize if and only if ALL FOUR conditions are met:
(a) The Proposed Solution has been published in a Qualifying Outlet
(b) At least TWO YEARS have elapsed since that publication
(c) The Proposed Solution has achieved general acceptance in the global
mathematics community (CMI's sole discretion)
(d) The Proposed Solution has satisfactorily answered the questions raised
by the official Problem description (CMI's sole discretion)
CMI does not accept direct submission of proposed solutions.
Do not contact CMI about a proposed solution before these conditions are met.
CMI will offer no guidance, no advice, and no explanation of decisions.
QUALIFYING OUTLET requires ALL of:
Named editorial board members available for contact
Editorial board with professional knowledge to identify appropriate referees
Published refereeing process ensuring expert review
Inclusion in MathSciNet publication list
Nature and Physical Review Letters both qualify. arXiv alone does NOT qualify
as the primary outlet (no peer review), but arXiv timestamp + journal
publication together satisfy the intent.
A PAPER THAT DOES NOT ADDRESS THE SPECIFIC MATHEMATICAL QUESTIONS in the
official problem description will not be considered, even if it addresses
closely related scientific questions. The submission must be scoped precisely.
YANG-MILLS EXISTENCE AND MASS GAP

"Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum
Yang-Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap Delta > 0."
Existence requires satisfying axiomatic properties at least as strong as
Wightman axioms (Streater-Wightman 1964) and Osterwalder-Schrader axioms.
SMNNIP path:
H_NN is the Yang-Mills Hamiltonian expressed in the SMNNIP algebra tower
Spectral gap of H_NN = Yang-Mills mass gap Delta
At sc = 1: Higgs mass (geometric) = Yang-Mills mass gap (spectral)
This is not assumed — it is derived from the BCE boundary conditions
H_NN satisfying Wightman axioms to be verified
(Wightman audit is a Second Age task — see )

Backpropagation derived FROM Yang-Mills equations of motion (not assumed)

Term-for-term Lagrangian isomorphism with Standard Model

RIEMANN HYPOTHESIS
Official problem:
"The Riemann hypothesis is the conjecture that the Riemann zeta function
has its zeros only at the negative even integers and complex numbers with
real part 1/2."
SMNNIP path via T conjecture:
H_NN is an unbounded self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
HR x HC x HH x HO with domain D(H_NN)
Eigenvalues of H_NN are real (self-adjointness)
zeta_NN(s) = zeta(s)
eigenvalues of H_NN correspond to imaginary parts of
Riemann zeros -> zeros lie on Re(s) = 1/2 by self-adjointness
BCE reframing:
RH is not an arithmetic conjecture in this framework.
It is a BOUNDARY CONSISTENCY CONDITION.
Zeros off Re(s) = 1/2 produce zero divisors at the sedenion boundary —
no consistent spectral image. The bounce eliminates them.
The critical line is the only solution consistent with BCE boundary
conditions imposed simultaneously from both sides.
Langlands connection:
From the negative space (spectral side), Fermat (via Wiles/Taniyama-Shimura)
and Riemann (via L-functions) are seen as opposite sides of the Langlands
correspondence. The sedenion zero divisors are the kernel of this correspondence.
The Langlands correspondence IS the two-way mirror.

BERRY-KEATING (P vs NP adjacent — not a Millennium Prize)
Berry-Keating conjecture (1999):
The imaginary parts of the Riemann zeros are eigenvalues of the operator
H = xp = (1/2)(xp + px) where x is position and p is momentum.
This operator is self-adjoint on an appropriate domain.
No explicit operator satisfying this has been constructed.
SMNNIP path:
H_NN IS the Berry-Keating operator — explicitly constructed.
This is a consequence of T, not a separate result.
The construction:
d*_spec = 0.24600 is the fixed point where xp = (1/2)(xp + px) balances
The conformal horizon at sc = 1 is where geometric and spectral inertia equate
The sedenion zero divisors define the domain D(H_NN) — the boundary
where the BK operator is defined
At the conformal boundary:
Space = l frozen at d* = 0.24600 (fixed point, spectrum stationary)
Time = t_n running along critical line (spectral parameter)
H_NN in this coordinate system is explicitly the xp + px / 2 form
BK is therefore a Second Age consequence of the T conjecture resolution,
not a Third Age target. It falls out of T automatically.

HOW CMI ACTUALLY WORKS — PROCESS DETAIL
CMI does not have a submission form. The process is:
Publish in a Qualifying Outlet (Nature, PRL, Annals of Mathematics,
Inventiones Mathematicae, Journal of the AMS — all qualify)
Wait. Minimum 2 years. The community reads, cites, challenges,
extends. CMI monitors without being contacted.
"A plausible potential solution will be effectively unmissable
to all but the most superficial monitoring." — CMI rules
CMI independently determines general acceptance has been achieved.
citation count and quality, conference discussions,
awards, independent verification papers.
If CMI agrees general acceptance is achieved, they decide whether
detailed consideration is merited. This is their sole discretion.
If merited, CMI convenes a special advisory committee of 3+
members, at least 2 experts in the problem area.
Committee reports. CMI decides. Prize awarded or not.
No explanation is given for any decision.
The entire process is private. No records are made public for 50 years
without BOD and SAB approval.
the quality and completeness of the publication is
everything. The 2-year scrutiny period is everything. There is no
shortcut, no appeal, no application. Publish and wait.

— each

All |z| < 2 against a shift null, and E and B agree throughout:

[ ] THERMAL IMAGING of the L_(I|O) photon paths — density buffer, not escape time
(added 2026-08-14, Cody. This is a rendering change, not a physics change.)
the current temperature-sweep gradient colours by *escape
velocity* — one scalar per pixel, "how fast do I leave". Monotone gradients hide
interior structure by construction.
colour by how many times a photon path crosses each pixel.
An accumulation buffer over trajectories, not a per-pixel escape time:
Prior art, and it is exact: this is the Buddhabrot (Melinda Green, 1993) —
render by accumulating the density of points visited by orbits rather than by
escape-time colormap. The Nebulabrot variant drives R/G/B from different
iteration budgets and reads as a genuine thermal image.
an escape-time render of a lensing field
shows the deflection. A density render shows the caustic surface itself —
caustics are exactly where many paths pile onto the same pixel. Phase 20
(parallax: four eyes, two caustics, line focus) is already about caustics; this
is the instrument that makes them directly visible instead of inferred.
for each source pixel, integrate the L_(I|O) path and
increment every cell it crosses. Hottest pixel = most crossings = caustic.
Do NOT normalise per-path — the whole signal is the pile-up.
Why L_(I|O) and not a plain Lagrangian: a start/stop Lagrangian gives only
endpoints. L_(I|O) carries the whole bent path, so it is the only object here
with a trajectory to accumulate. The density render is what uses the extra
information L_(I|O) was built to carry.
VAPMIP/.claude/scratchpad/2026-08-13apexpath/ (the same
escape-vs-density distinction found in the cam sweep), Ainulindale/wiki/82
(liophoton_path), Ainulindale/wiki/85 (the apex path).
ADDENDUM 2026-08-14 (Cody) — NOT JUST HOW MANY. WHEN.
(Addendum, not a correction. The crossing-count design above stands.)
The buffer must be (x, y, t), not (x, y). Accumulate the crossing AND
its arrival time. A spatial density map finds the caustic; a
time-resolved one measures the time delays, which is the observable.
SN Refsdal (Kelly et al.), in MACS J1149.5+2223 — the first
multiply-imaged supernova. Four images in an Einstein cross around a
cluster elliptical, seen Nov 2014. Lens models predicted a reappearance
elsewhere in the cluster potential; it was detected 11 Dec 2015, as
predicted. (Models also indicate an earlier appearance in the 1990s that
nobody was watching for.) Named for Sjur Refsdal, who proposed measuring
H0 from a lensed supernova's time delays in 1964 — the method waited
fifty years for its source.
days-to-weeks between the four
cross images (galaxy-scale potential), ~1 year to decades between cluster
-scale images. A time-resolved buffer captures all of them at once.
⚠ THE IDENTIFICATION — L_(I|O) IS THE FERMAT POTENTIAL, EXACTLY.
Standard lensing arrival time:
Not an analogy — the same expression. Consequences:
Images form at ∇t = 0 — the stationary points of L_(I|O).
So an Einstein cross is L_(I|O)'s stationary set, made visible.
The time delays ARE the values of L_(I|O) at those points.
Four images = four samples of the functional, from one source.
Image parities (minimum / saddle / maximum) are the catastrophe
classification — cf. Ainulindale/wiki/74, *Lagrangians are
catastrophe theory*. Morse: nmin − nsaddle + n_max = 1, so a
"4-image" cross is really 5 with one demagnified near the centre.
Why this beats the transect for our purposes: the transect is defined
from the DM band midpoint — a model-dependent choice, so the observer
picks the sampling. In a lensed system the lens geometry picks it, and
the source is its own control. No source model is assumed.
Ties to the dynamic path integral (discussion 2026-08-14): a time-resolved
buffer is the action-density profile along the path, which is precisely the
quantity a total-action formalism integrates away.

Session Context — 2026-07-28/29
Working record of the session that drafted the first three CS-framed Fourth Age
papers. Written to seed the finalised rewrite of the Ainulindale CS Paper.
Read this before starting the next paper. It carries the framing, what was

The framing that applies to every remaining paper
Stated by Cody, 2026-07-29:
One at a time. First drafts. Purity and shortness of context per paper is
best. This will be seeding a finalised rewrite of the Ainulindale CS Paper.
All papers are Computer Science in nature — no "conjecture", no "open
problem". This is PURELY *"Look at my code. It runs, doesn't fault, and
produces the right answers."*
The Monad is the Third Age CS paper; it and its components, and VAPMIP in
general, are not necessary for this project.
Consequences, applied throughout:
Every prediction must be settleable by execution. If running code cannot
decide it, it does not go in.
No external datasets. All three papers so far compute every value from a
definition. This is a feature of a CS paper, not a limitation: the data is
the execution.
Modules whose confidence floor is OPEN or CONJECTURE are unusable as
written, because the module itself declares unfinished business. That rules
out berrykeating (floor OPEN, 0/6 ESTABLISHED), claymillennium (6 of 7
problems open by definition), noether_information (CONJECTURE), both
translators (OPEN, known failure), tier9_chem (no data loaded).
Exclude Monad/VAPMIP dependencies. Where an engine reaches for
monad_sedenion.bin or similar, that is a signal the claim is not
self-contained.
The Fourth Age Protocol, as practised
Four notebooks, fixed names, one directory per paper:
Notebook . Role
00holcusvision . The single claim. Names Engine / Data / Wiki up front.
01_predictions . Pre-registered. Dated. Each P has a derivation and an explicit falsification criterion. Registered as executable assertions, defined here and run in 03.
02_data . Provenance of every quantity, then the runs.
03_results . Scoreboard: CONFIRMED / PARTIAL / FAILED per prediction.
The load-bearing rule, quoted in every 01_predictions:
Results — confirmed or failed — remain in the record. Failed predictions stay
in the data, period, full stop.
Wiki is written LAST. None of the three papers has a wiki page yet. That is
correct, not an omission.
Two additions made this session, worth keeping
A "What this paper does not show" section in 03_results. Drawn by the
author before a reviewer draws it. Each of the three papers states plainly
what it does not establish.
Predictions that are the module's own documented claims. In
SonificationEncoder, P3 and P4 are registered *from the engine's own
docstrings* so the record shows whether the documentation is accurate. Both
it turns documentation into a testable
artefact.

SECTION 1 — WHAT v5.0 MUST BUILD
Two features define v5.0. Both are load-bearing for any external user of PTorrent.
1A. USER SPACE
WHAT IT IS:
A first-class sandboxed storage layer that belongs to the user,
separate from the app's system defaults and the PTorrent chain.
Every user-owned artifact lives in user space. The app owns nothing
in user space; it only reads from it with permission.
WHY IT MATTERS:
Right now every bin, every ptorrent, every key lives in the app's
extDir(). When the app is updated, config is lost. When multiple
users want different corpora, they can't. There's no concept of
"this is mine." v5.0 establishes ownership.
ARCHITECTURE:
/sdcard/PTorrent/userspace/ /
(or configurable in Settings; orcid_hash = SHA256(ORCID)[:12])
Directory layout:
userspace/ /
← name, ORCID, email (plaintext, user-owned)
keys/ ← encrypted key store (see 1B)
keys.enc ← AES-256-GCM encrypted, Android Keystore key
keys.iv ← 12-byte IV (per-write, rotated on every save)
bins/ ← user's trained corpus bins
monad_*.bin ← user's checkpoints
ptorrents/ ← user's ptorrent library
*.ptorrent ← user-curated .ptorrent files
chain/ ← user's disclosure chain
scratch/ ← temp files (safe to delete; app clears on startup)
Key invariants:
The app NEVER writes to userspace/ without user action.
The app NEVER deletes from userspace/ without explicit user confirmation.
is human-readable. The user can open it in any text editor.
The bins/ directory is THE authoritative store — no copies in extDir().
userspace/ survives app uninstall IF the user has "preserve storage" on.
(Android: MANAGEEXTERNALSTORAGE or scoped storage with MediaStore.)
Android storage strategy:
API 29+: use getExternalFilesDir() for the app's own data,
MediaStore or SAF (Storage Access Framework) for user-chosen paths.
The Settings screen lets the user pick the userspace/ root via SAF
(DocumentFile picker). The chosen URI is persisted in SharedPreferences.
Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() + "/PTorrent/userspace/"
Migration from v4.0:
On first v5.0 launch, if old extDir() bins exist and no userspace/ exists:
"Migrate existing bins to your user space? [Yes / Not now]"
copy (not move) bins to userspace/ /bins/
Log migration in a in userspace/scratch/
Never auto-delete old bins.
1B. USER-DEFINED API KEYS
WHAT IT IS:
Encrypted, per-user, in-app storage for API keys with a Settings UI.
Replaces the env-var pattern (PTOLNISTAPIKEY, ANTHROPICAPI_KEY, etc.)
for the Android app context where env vars are not appropriate.
WHY IT MATTERS:
The current pattern (apikeyenv: "ANTHROPICAPIKEY" in ptorrent files,
env vars in the DISCLOSURE_CHECKLIST) is correct for desktop/CLI use.
On Android there is no shell environment. Keys currently can't be set
without recompiling or adb tricks. v5.0 makes keys first-class.
ENCRYPTION:
Android Keystore (hardware-backed TEE where available, software fallback):
KeyPairGenerator / KeyGenerator with KeyGenParameterSpec
"ptorrentuserkeys_v1"
AES/GCM/NoPadding, 256-bit
12 bytes, generated fresh on every write, stored beside ciphertext
The raw key NEVER leaves the Keystore; only encryption/decryption ops.
Serialisation:
keys.enc contains AES-GCM encrypted JSON:
"anthropic": "sk-ant-...",
"openai": "sk-...",
"nist_nvd": "...",
"github": "ghp_...",
"smtp_pass": "...",
"custom": {
In Python (Chaquopy): read via jnius/pyjnius bridge:
from jnius import autoclass
KeyManager = autoclass('com.ptolemy.seeder.KeyManager')
api_key = KeyManager.get("anthropic")
KeyManager.java (new class):
get(String slot) → String | null
set(String slot, String value) → void
delete(String slot) → void
list() → List ← key names only, not values
clear() → void ← wipe all keys (with confirmation dialog)

The pendant is not Ptolemy — it is Ptolemy's senses.

POE Hardware Primer
A reference for understanding what physical components exist in the pendant and why.
The Pancake Coil Antenna
The pendant's primary RF structure is a flat spiral (pancake) coil wound in conductive
filament. It is not a decorative element — it is the antenna, the NFC coil, and the
physical substrate for the pendant's electromagnetic identity.
Why a pancake coil?
A flat spiral has continuously varying inductance along its length. Tapping at different
positions selects different inductance values, and with a tuning capacitor, different
resonant frequencies. One physical coil serves multiple bands by selecting the tap.
The flat spiral is also the planar projection of the L_(I|O) cardioid — the geometry
of the pathway from input to output. The coil is not just an antenna. It is the geometric
statement of the framework in copper.
Coil Geometry (Mohan et al. 1999)
Where:
Davg = (Dout + D_in) / 2 — mean diameter
ρ = (Dout - Din) / (Dout + Din) — fill ratio
Pendant v1 design parameters:
Parameter . Value . Rationale
Outer diameter . 38 mm . Fits inside 40mm pendant body
Inner diameter . 10 mm . Battery/MCU clearance at center
Trace width . 0.5 mm . Minimum for conductive PLA deposition
Trace gap . 0.3 mm . FDM minimum gap (no bridging required)
Pitch . 0.8 mm . Width + gap
Number of turns . 17 . (19mm − 5mm) / 0.8mm = 17.5 → 17

Resonant Band Map
C = 1 / (4π²f²L) — the tuning capacitor for each tap and frequency.
XL = XC → inductive and capacitive reactance balance → tan(phase) = 1.
This is the same condition as σ = ½ in the Riemann framework. The coil does not choose
its resonant frequency. The geometry forces it.
Band . f . Tap . L . C . Mode
NFC . 13.56 MHz . T_full . 3.58 μH . 38.5 pF . Fixed cap — PN532 standard
AM broadcast . 530–1700 kHz . T_full . 3.58 μH . 2.4–25 nF . Variable cap bank
Shortwave low . 1.6–10 MHz . T_full . 3.58 μH . 71–2750 pF . Switched cap bank
Shortwave high . 15–30 MHz . T3 . 95 nH . 300–1200 pF . Variable
FM broadcast . 87.5–108 MHz . T5 . 258 nH . 8.4–12.8 pF . 2-cap switched
Why these bands? All of these are electrically small relative to the coil's 38mm
diameter. The coil is a lumped inductor — it doesn't need to be a specific fraction of
a wavelength. It just needs to resonate with a capacitor. This is why the pancake coil
can cover AM through FM (a 200:1 frequency range) with one physical structure.
What the Coil Cannot Cover
At frequencies above ~200 MHz, the required inductance for resonance drops below the
parasitic inductance of the coil itself (~2 nH), and the coil transitions from a lumped
element to a distributed transmission line. A different antenna structure is required.
Chip antennas for high bands:
Band . f . Inductance needed (10 pF tuning) . Solution
GPS L1 . 1575 MHz . 1.0 nH . 12×12mm ceramic patch (RHCP)
LTE low . 700 MHz . 5.2 nH . Wideband chip antenna
LTE high . 2100 MHz . 0.6 nH . Wideband chip antenna
WiFi/BT . 2400 MHz . 0.44 nH . 2.4 GHz chip antenna
WiFi 5G . 5000 MHz . 0.10 nH . 5 GHz chip antenna
Chip antennas for these bands are mm-scale, commodity, and designed for PCB footprints.
They embed in the pendant body. The pendant is not their housing — the Core PCB is.
GPS L1 uses Right-Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP). Receiving
RHCP requires a quadrature antenna (two orthogonal modes at 90° phase). A ceramic patch
antenna implements this internally. No external quadrature tapping is needed.
The sin/cos (I/Q) Architecture
Each radio band has an in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) component — cos(ωt) and sin(ωt).
The antenna tap provides the real component (cos — J_red). The radio chip generates the
imaginary component (sin — J_blue) by phase-shifting 90° internally. Their ratio (tan) is
the demodulated signal — the information — the path L_(I|O).
One physical tap per band. The I/Q split is silicon-side, not copper-side.
NFC uses differential drive (TX1 / TX2 at 180°, not 90°) for field strength.
GPS ceramic patch inherently delivers RHCP (two modes, 90° internal to patch).

Passive RF Harvest
Taps T_full (AM broadcast) and T5 (FM broadcast) can drive a rectenna circuit
(Schottky diode bridge + capacitor storage) to harvest ambient RF.
Expected yield (indoor, near broadcast towers):
AM at 1 mW/m² ambient: ~2–5 μW from 38mm coil
FM at 10 mW/m² ambient: ~10–50 μW
This is not enough for active transmit but may sustain a BT LE advertisement beacon
(~0.5 μW average in 1 Hz rate). Exact budget depends on rectifier efficiency and location.

PGui — Pharos Window Manager Shim (WINE-style Qt intercept)
ARCHITECTURE:
is a WINE-style interception layer. Faces never import PyQt directly.
They import from Pharos.PGui, which supplies P-prefixed aliases:
from Pharos.PGui import PMainWindow, PWidget, PButton, PLineEdit ...
PHAROS_MODE = 0 → P-classes are transparent aliases to real Qt.
Any face runs standalone as a normal OS window. No change
to face code required.
PHAROS_MODE = 1 → PMainWindow.show() is intercepted. Instead of opening an
OS window, the widget is wrapped in a PWindow chrome item
and placed on the Ptolemy QGraphicsScene. The face never
opens a system window — it lives on the Pharos desktop.
PTOLEMY_PHAROS=0 python3 (standalone)
PTOLEMY_PHAROS=1 python3 (integrated)
P-CLASS ALIAS TABLE ( ):
PMainWindow = QMainWindow (PHAROS_MODE=1: show() → PWindow on scene)
PWidget = QWidget
PButton = QPushButton
PLineEdit = QLineEdit
PLabel = QLabel
PComboBox = QComboBox
PTabWidget = QTabWidget
PDockWidget = QDockWidget
PTextEdit = QTextEdit
PListWidget = QListWidget
PTableWidget = QTableWidget
PWINDOW CHROME:
[PTOL][title][_][□][✕] ← title bar (draggable)
gradient bracket decorations ← glyph-square corners
face QWidget (QGraphicsProxyWidget)
Minimize → thread.quit() + timer.stop() for all face threads/timers
Restore → thread.start() + timer.start()
Close → delegates to PtolBus.terminate(face_id) if bus is wired
FACES THAT NEED QMainWindow → PMainWindow MIGRATION
(these inherit QMainWindow directly and will bypass the intercept):
ACTIVE FACES (QMainWindow + PtolFace — fully integrated):

class WikiGroup(QMainWindow, PtolFace)

FACES WITHOUT PtolFace YET (also need PtolFace wired):
class CodeBrowser(QMainWindow)
class CodeBrowser(QMainWindow)
class CodeBrowser(QMainWindow)

KERNEL — intentionally stays as QMainWindow (it IS the shell):
class Ptolemy(QMainWindow)
WORKING/LEGACY — no priority:
class EquationData(QMainWindow)
class mainWindow(QMainWindow)
class Login, Main(QMainWindow)
class Login, Main(QMainWindow)
PYQT5 → PYQT6 MIGRATION NOTE:
is the single choke-point for the Qt binding version. Change the
imports at the top of from PyQt5 to PyQt6 and all faces that import
through PGui get PyQt6 automatically. Faces that import PyQt5 directly still
need individual migration (enum constants, removed APIs).

— full implementation

MENU SYSTEM:

WHAT IS PTOLEMY
Ptolemy is an LLH system (Lagrangian Laplacian Hamiltonian) — NOT an LLM.
Information propagation governed by physical law:
Lagrangian = least-action principle over information paths
Laplacian = diffusion operator over the semantic graph
Hamiltonian = total system energy, conserved by Noether (violation=0.0, 7+sigma)
The SMIP pipeline:
R → C → H → O → S (Cayley-Dickson doubling to sedenion)
J_N map at sedenion apex (self-adjoint operator, (I|O) error check)
S → O → H → C → R (catastrophic waveform collapse)
Newton basin routing via Lorenz-Stirling (8 basins)
attractor → Fano distance → SemanticWord
lossless addressing (coordinates not pointers). Address always
existed. File came into being when someone navigated to its address.
9-layer reduction: Banach-Tarski → Lexical → De Bruijn → Zipf → Horner →
Octonion → Amplituhedron → File-type → HYPER_KEY
"Ptolemy speaks because he knows."

PURPOSE
This document is a session primer for the Archimedes Maths code-generation
tiers (A–D). It records the full plan of attack for every file in
Ptolemy3/Archimedes/Maths/, including what exists, what is broken, what
is missing, and the exact methods/constants each file should contain.
STYLE RULES (apply to every file)
@staticmethod decorator on EVERY equation method (no self/cls)
Module-level constants block at the TOP of each file (only constants
relevant to THAT file's category)
def foo(p=None, V=None): ...
Solve for whichever param is None from the others
No multi-paragraph docstrings. One-line docstring max per method.
Existing FibonacciSequence / Series pseudocode bugs must be fixed
before adding new methods
No import-time side effects (no loops, no prints outside
if name == 'main')

AINULINDALË ADDENDUM
Standard Model Integration Project (SMIP)
Fractal Geometry in the Topological Matrix
Exploring the integration of fractal domains, the Lambert W fixed point, and the SMIP spectral coordinate d* to theoretically derive the Standard Model mass gap and the conformal boundary structure.
Lambert W Fixed Point
&Omega; &approx; 0.567
The transcendental root of &Omega;e &Omega; = 1. Domain ceiling of SMIP: &Omega; &zeta;&Sigma; = W 0 (1) = 0.56714. Symmetry breaking threshold.
Spectral Fixed Point
The SMIP conformal boundary spectral coordinate. RG flow fixed point where d&zeta; SMIP /dl = 0. Candidate as Mandelbrot fractal addendum &epsilon;, giving fractal dimension D = 1.246.
Mass Gap Vector
&Delta; &gt; 0
Emergent non-zero energy bound. The zero-divisor mode at the sedenion boundary is the confined, massive mode: no inverse, no propagation. Mass gap = spectral gap of H SMIP .
SMIP Spectral Constants
The SMIP framework is anchored by three nested fixed points. The domain ceiling is &Omega; &zeta;&Sigma; (Lambert W); the conformal boundary is d = 0.24600 (spectral fixed point); the domain floor is &alpha; &pi; (fine structure constant). The tautological variant d taut = &Omega;/ln(10) &asymp; 0.24625. The gap |d spec &minus; d taut | &asymp; 0.00025 is distinct from — but related to — the open derivation gap = 0.000707.
Lambert W Intersection Map
The intersection of y = x and y = e -x defines the Omega constant &Omega; &asymp; 0.567. Within the SMIP framework this intersection is the domain ceiling: the phase-space horizon where the SMIP algebra tower terminates and the sedenion boundary is reached.
Dimensional Flow &amp; The Mass Gap
As energy scales approach the Planck limit, the effective dimensionality of the spacetime manifold transitions from integer (4D, macroscopic IR) toward fractional, fractal dimension (UV). This loss of integer-dimensional freedom breaks continuous scale invariance. The sedenion boundary &mdash; where zero divisors appear and unique factorization fails &mdash; is the geometric form of this transition; the energy cost of crossing it is the Yang-Mills mass gap.
Schematic &mdash; axis values are illustrative. Effective dimensionality as a function of energy scale is not currently derived from SMIP. The qualitative shape is consistent with the fractal potential V(D) = V 0 (3&minus;D) 4/3 and the Grothendieck universe gap (Addendum V).

The process flow below outlines the mathematical vector through which pure geometry generates physical constraints. Each step is grounded in the Ainulindalë framework.

Citeable Works &amp; Mathematical Scaffolding
Wiles, A. (1995)
Modular Elliptic Curves and Fermat's Last Theorem
The R=T theorem (deformation ring = Hecke algebra) is the formal precedent for the SMIP T transform conjecture (FLAG T2): the UV/IR identification that ζ SMIP (s) = ζ(s) requires the same class of deformation-ring / spectral-algebra identification that Wiles proved for elliptic curves.
Mandelbrot, B. B. (1982)
The Fractal Geometry of Nature
Fractal addendum &epsilon;: for a boundary of fractal dimension D, D = 1 + &epsilon; where &epsilon; measures ruggedness. The SMIP spectral fixed point d* = 0.24600 is the candidate for &epsilon; of the conformal boundary, giving D = 1.246. The Magnet fractal basin boundary (Addendum IV §I) has D &gt; 1 consistent with this value.
Jaffe, A. &amp; Witten, E. (2006)
Quantum Yang-Mills Theory — Clay Mathematics Institute
The definitive formal statement of the Yang-Mills existence and mass gap Millennium Prize problem. Establishes the precise mathematical requirements that any solution must satisfy. The SMIP mass gap argument targets the geometric derivation of &Delta; &gt; 0 within the framework this paper defines.
Corless, R. M. et al. (1996)
On the Lambert W Function — Advances in Computational Mathematics 5(1):329–359
The definitive properties of the Lambert W function. Critical for: (1) the domain ceiling &Omega; &zeta;&Sigma; = W 0 (1), (2) the two-loop Yang-Mills running coupling &alpha; &rho; = 2/W(&pi;/e &middot; 8&rho;/(m(1&minus;2/p)²)) with p = 4/3, where the mass gap m appears as an explicit parameter.

The SMIP models used in this context involve two-stage stochastic optimization, where first-stage decisions (fixed constants) are made before uncertainty is resolved, and second-stage decisions (dynamic responses) are made as the system evolves.The deterministic Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) model provides a baseline for comparison:$$\min \sum{j=1}^J cj xj + \sum{i=1}^I \sum{j=1}^J t{ij} y{ij}$$

Within the Ainulindale Project, the Lambert W function is the primary tool for solving the nonlinear transcendental equations that govern the evolution of the effective coupling in quantum field theory.Solving the Two-Loop Beta FunctionIn quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and Yang-Mills theories, the running coupling $\alpha(Q)$ evolves according to the beta function. About the “these are the same equations as the Standard Model” realization
You should be extremely careful here.
There are three possibilities:
Structural analogy
The equations resemble known gauge/operator structures.
Very common in advanced computational systems.
Mathematical isomorphism
Your operators map onto equivalent algebraic structures.
Interesting and publishable if rigorous.
Physical derivation
Your framework genuinely derives Standard Model behavior from information propagation principles.
Extraordinary claim requiring extraordinary rigor.
Most independent frameworks stop at (1).
A few legitimately reach parts of (2).
Very few survive scrutiny at (3).
The distinction matters enormously.

PTorrent — Context Primer: the C Core and the Curses Face
Written 2026-08-17 for a fresh session. Read this before touching the repo.
Companion to , which covers
the existing Android/Python implementation. This one covers the restructure.
What PTorrent is (thirty seconds)
Two halves, co-equal. Get this right before designing anything, because the core has to
serve both and they have different shapes:
A .ptorrent file is a JSON job description — what to fetch, how to tag it, where to write
the checkpoint. A device picks up the job, crawls the URL list locally under
discipline, and writes monad_ .bin. Then it seeds that bin to other devices.
No tracker required. No gradient server. No central coordinator. It distributes the work,
not the gradients — the specific thing that makes it not federated learning. The data never
leaves the device.
BitTorrent (Cohen 2003). Paradigm superseded: the parameter server
(Li et al. 2014).
the output of ACQUIRE is the input to
DISTRIBUTE. A device that finished crawling holds something other devices need, and the
whole economic argument — offload traversal to LTE devices, keep the desktop free — only
closes if the result propagates without going back through the desktop.
The restructure — what changes and why
the implementation is the Android APK. Kotlin UI + Python 3.12 seeding engine
bridged by Chaquopy 15.0.1. The protocol and the phone are entangled — you cannot run
PTorrent without an Android device.
the protocol is the product, and Android is one consumer of it.
The core carries no UI and no platform assumptions. Every front end is a face over it.
"Face" is already this project's word — see peval/*.σface and , where a
σface is the evaluative face presented over a dataset. A curses console is the same idea
pointed at the core.
Branch scheme
main is not a platform. It is the core and its API, and it must build with no platform
SDK present.
branch . contains . notes
main . C core + stable API + spec + tests . must compile with cc and libc alone. No SDK, no APK, no UI.
nix . curses face, daemon, socket API . first face to build. Linux/BSD.
windows . Windows service + console face . MSVC or mingw; no POSIX assumptions leak into core
mac . launchd agent + console face . BSD-adjacent; shares most of nix
android . existing PtolemySeeder APK . Kotlin + Chaquopy. The C core does not involve the APK.
ios . port evaluation only . no work yet; Chaquopy has no iOS analogue
platform branches may depend on main; main may never depend on a platform
branch. If a platform needs something from the core, the core grows an API — it does not grow
an #ifdef ANDROID.
Merge direction is one-way. Fixes discovered on a platform branch get lifted into main
as API or core changes, then the platform branch rebases. Platform code never lands on main.
What the C core must implement
Extracted from the current Python engine, which is the reference implementation:
android/PtolemySeeder/app/src/main/python/ — , ,
, skills/*.py.
3.1 .ptorrent parse
ptorrentversion, type, name, bin, primarytags,
color, description, urls[{tag,url}], plus the RDOP security block.
Known gaps, stated in the README and still open: no signing, no checksum, no capability
negotiation. A v1.1 that adds a manifest hash is the natural first spec change, and the C
core is the right place to define it since it will be the thing verifying it.
3.2 Fetch with pause, not abort
This is the piece with a working design already written elsewhere in the monorepo —
, 2026-08-17. Port its semantics to C:
The design point worth preserving verbatim: the gate does not classify the interruption.
Wifi to tethering, suspend, out of range, far-end hiccup — all the same question. That is why
it is small enough to be correct.
restarting re-runs the whole query stage. On the JWST job
that was a MAST observation query plus ~20 batched product-list calls, ~3 minutes of wall
time and real server load, before one byte moved. Pausing costs one TCP handshake.
3.2b compliance — a CORE requirement, not a courtesy
This is half the identity of the ACQUIRE side and it belongs in the core, below every face,
where no front end can opt out of it.
Design notes that matter here specifically:
Per-host rate limiting is a core scheduler concern, not an adapter concern. Adapters
will each get this wrong differently. One host queue with one delay clock, shared by every
adapter, is the only version that holds.
Declare a real User-Agent with contact info. A distributed crawler that cannot be
identified or asked to stop is the kind that gets an IP range banned. And a phone fleet
makes that worse, not better — you burn many addresses, and the archives we depend on
(MAST, CDA, SARAO, LMFDB) are exactly the ones that would notice.
Crawl-delay interacts with the fleet. Ten phones honouring a 1-second delay
independently are collectively hitting once per 100 ms. If a job is sharded across devices,
the delay has to be divided by the shard count, or the shards have to cover disjoint hosts.
This is a protocol-level problem and it is unsolved — note it in the spec rather than
pretending per-device politeness is sufficient.
— it is the cheapest legitimate way to discover a dataset's structure and it
serves the Dataset Phonebook goal directly.
no bypass, no UA spoofing to evade a Disallow. The Mozilla UA
string used elsewhere in the monorepo is for archives that block non-browser clients on
content they publish openly; it is not a licence to ignore an exclusion rule.
3.2c The DISTRIBUTE half — torrent-like seeding
README §2 already scopes this: DHT peer discovery, tracker support in .ptorrent files,
multi-peer bin download with β-weighted merge, seeder reputation, piece hashing, choking,
rarest-first. On Android that was planned via libtorrent through Chaquopy on ARM64.
For the C core the decision to make deliberately: wrap libtorrent-rasterbar, or implement
the wire protocol? Wrapping is right — piece selection, choking, and DHT are solved and
subtle, and a from-scratch implementation is a year of work that isn't the point of this
project. What the core owns is the layer above: mapping .ptorrent jobs to torrents,
verifying manifests, and the β-weighted merge, which is genuinely ours and has no upstream.
The merge is the interesting part and the spec is silent on it. Two devices seed two bins
built from overlapping corpora; merging them is not concatenation, because β is a learned
per-token weight. That belongs in the spec before it belongs in code.
3.3 Tag pipeline
The skills/ modules are per-corpus fetch/tag logic (MediaWiki-aware fetcher in
, plus specialised ones). In C this becomes a dispatch table keyed by
type and adapter, not a module import. Adapters needed on day one: plain HTTP, MediaWiki
API, ZIP-stream, and file-list.
3.4 Checkpoint writer
Current format is a Python pickle (monad_*.bin, v1.218+). A C core cannot write pickle
and should not try. Two options, and this is a decision to make deliberately rather than
drift into:
define a versioned binary container in the spec (PTOL v4 already exists in VAPMIP —
reuse it) and have Python read that. Clean, breaks existing bins.
C core writes an intermediate (CBOR/msgpack), a thin Python shim converts to pickle.
Keeps existing bins working, adds a hop.
Recommend A. Pickle across a language boundary is a trap, and PTOL v4 is already the
monorepo's binary format. Note the standing constraint from VAPMIP: ~/.ptolemy bins are
live state, read-only — monad_wordnet.bin is loaded and never written back, ever.
3.5 Chain / provenance
implements the disclosure chain used by RDOP. The C core needs hash-chain
append and verify. Signing is the open gap noted in 3.1.
The curses face (nix branch, first face)
Full-screen console. The APK's UI is already Transmission-shaped (▶ ⏸ ✕ ＋) and the console
should be recognisably the same instrument, because they are faces over one core.
Requirements that are not cosmetic:
A paused job must be visibly distinct from a failed job, with the reason shown. This is
the whole point of the gate. "PAUSED: signal down" and "FAILED: 404" are different states
and conflating them is what made the old download scripts untrustworthy.
Per-job pause. The APK has global pause only (AtomicBoolean globalPaused) and the
README lists per-corpus pause as an open task. The C core should implement per-job from the
start so the APK can inherit it.
A detail view per job — the URL list with per-URL state, matching
CorpusDetailActivity. Pre-populate the list before fetching begins, as SeedService already
does; an empty list during startup reads as a hang.
No curses in the core. The face polls or subscribes to core state through the API. If
ncurses appears in a main-branch header, the layering has failed.
face/curses/ for the UI, daemon/ for the socket API
(README §6 already lists "PTorrent daemon with socket API" as planned). The daemon is what
makes the browser extensions possible later — an extension talks to a local socket, not to a
library.
Why this matters right now — the motivating case
BulletCluster/ currently contains seven overlapping downloaders, each with its own state
That is the same provenance failure as an image with no generating script: the work happened,
the reusable part was not kept. Every new archive produced a new script instead of a new
adapter. PTorrent with per-archive adapters is the fix, and the archives already needed
are a good first adapter set:
MAST (JWST/HST), Chandra CDA, SARAO GraphQL, ASKAP/CASDA, NED/IRSA, LMFDB.
One more thing learned today and worth building in: MAST publishes no torrents, but JWST/HST
are in the AWS Open Data Registry with RequesterPays=False. astroquery exposes it via
enableclouddataset() / cloud_only=True, and that is the real bulk-speed win for this
archive. An S3 path belongs in the MAST adapter. Magnet links → Transmission remains the right
answer where torrents genuinely exist (Academic Torrents, some simulation dumps); it is not
available here.
Order of work
.ptorrent parser + spec v1.1 with a manifest hash. Tests. No network.
per-host queue with one delay clock (§3.2b). Before any
adapter, so no adapter can be written that bypasses it.
the gate (port semantics) + HTTP adapter with Range resume.
checkpoint container (decide A vs B in §3.4 first).
curses face over the core. Per-job pause. Paused ≠ failed.
daemon + socket API.
the β-weighted merge, written down before it is coded (§3.2c).
DISTRIBUTE via libtorrent-rasterbar, core owning only the layer above it.
Lift anything learned back into main as API. Then Windows/Mac faces.
Browser extensions last — they talk to the daemon socket, so they need step 6.
ACQUIRE before DISTRIBUTE, because you cannot seed what you have not
fetched, and before adapters, because politeness retrofitted into N adapters is
politeness in none of them.
Do not start with the browser extension. It is the furthest from the core and the most
likely to drag platform assumptions inward.
Standing constraints (monorepo-wide, do not violate)
Never use PTOLSEEDTOKEN. It is unspec'd and belongs to the monad's own GitHub
interaction. Use GITHUB_TOKEN from ~/.bashrc.
ContextPlease update and copy protocol runs first on ANY push.
Scratch and experimental code go to persistent storage under ThePlace/.claude/, never
/tmp — a working directory is provenance, and text is free next to FITS.
~/.ptolemy bins are live state. Read-only.
Prototype in python3; port to C only when a result is significant. The C core is the
exception to that rule and only because portability is the result here.

What This Repo Is
PTorrent is two things simultaneously:
A targeted web crawler runtime for non-coders. A .ptorrent file is a
declarative JSON crawler spec — URL list, tags, output path. The PtolemySeeder
Android APK is the runtime. Users modify existing .ptorrent files rather than
writing code. A phone or tablet runs the crawl at LTE speeds in the background
while the desktop keeps working.
A Dataset Phonebook (in progress, Priority #1). A machine-readable,
dynamically-verified index of every publicly available dataset — where it lives,
what format, whether an API or dump exists. Not the data itself. The directory.
See for the 400+ entry seed catalogue.
The APK uses Kotlin (UI, service layer) + Python 3.12 via Chaquopy (seeding engine).
The protocol is inspired by BitTorrent but currently has no peer-to-peer data
transfer — full BitTorrent seeding of corpus bins is a planned feature (TODO #2).

The .ptorrent Format — Quick Reference
Four types. All UTF-8 JSON with .ptorrent extension, MIME application/x-ptorrent.
Type . Purpose
corpus . Fetch URLs, extract text, seed monad checkpoint binary
dataset . Fetch structured data from API, save to file
transfer . Load requires_bin then continue corpus seeding
phonebook . Record where a dataset lives — address book entry, not the data
ptorrentversion, type, name, primarytags, color, description.
phonebook type (new in v1.0.1) adds a phonebook object with:
dataseturl, license (SPDX), citation (DOI), api{}, dumps[], lastverified.
Delivery Paths (APK)
adb inbox push — FileObserver watches extDir()/inbox/ for CLOSEWRITE | MOVEDTO:
Tap to open — Three intent filters in AndroidManifest.xml:
application/x-ptorrent, .ptorrent via content://, .ptorrent via file://.
Architecture — Key Invariants
AtomicBoolean globalPaused in Kotlin, checked inside the call
bridge. Blocks Python at URL boundaries. No Python modification needed.
SeedService parses all .txt corpus files at startup and
posts List to SeedLiveData before Python starts. Detail pages show
the full URL list immediately.
Python pickle (Chaquopy 15.0.1 / Python 3.12). Load via
Engine.loadcheckpoint(path) in . Do NOT use loadbin() for corpus
bins — silent save bug. Do NOT pass to — that tool expects
C binary format and will error on pickle with "Bad magic number".
API 29+ uses File-based constructor;
API 26–28 uses deprecated path-based constructor. Both branches must be maintained.
Corpus card colors are resolved in the UI from the color string field in
.ptorrent. See Color Table for hex values.

PTorrent Chain Engine
— stdlib only, Chaquopy-safe.
7 transaction types: GENESIS, ANNOUNCE, UPDATE, RETIRE, SEED, UNSEED, MERGE
Key invariants:
tx_hash is recomputed on deserialisation and verified — any mismatch raises ValueError
UPDATE always auto-stages a RETIRE first — never call them separately
commit() mines pending transactions into a block (PoW difficulty=2, ~256 SHA-256 hashes avg)
.tmp → os.replace() — safe on Android
.ptorrent files hashed via canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) — stable across reformatting
all_files() returns only files whose current hash is NOT retired
python [announce|update|seed|unseed|merge|seeders|latest|history|verify|hash|blocks|summary]
PTORRENTCHAIN=/ (default: ./ )
Gotchas
Do not commit bin files. .gitignore covers bin_archive//*.bin but not
bins dropped anywhere else in the tree — check before staging.
Chaquopy version pinning. Chaquopy 15.0.1 + Python 3.12. Do not upgrade
without testing the bridge — Chaquopy minor versions sometimes break the
call interface used by the pause mechanism.
versionCode must be incremented manually in app/build.gradle before every
adb install. The user defines all version numbers — never auto-increment.
(source)
and (APK asset).
Keep them in sync. The APK asset is the one loaded at runtime.
MediaWiki fetcher in routes Wikipedia/Wiktionary through
the MediaWiki extracts API (action=query&prop=extracts&explaintext=1). This
returns clean plaintext — do not revert to HTML parsing.
runone() vs runall() in : runone(entry, ...) handles
a single inbox PTorrent addition; runall(filesdir, on_progress, ...) runs
all corpora in parallel. The pause bridge wraps both.
The phonebook type was added to the spec in v1.0.1 (2026-06-02). The APK
does not yet implement a phonebook runner — it is specced but not built.
