WOULD HELP — not blocking
Published κ from Clowe+2006 / Bradač+2006. Not on disk. Needed for comparison against a
literature-accepted mass map. The Clowe Σ-map is 185 × 185 px at 8.5 kpc/pixel; I found no
clean archive download, so it likely means contacting the authors.
ALMA/VLA polarimetry of a polarized background source behind the cluster — the
differential-Faraday path (precedent: PKS 1830−211, ALMA differential polarimetry between
two lensed images, RM to a few × 10⁵ rad m⁻²). Requires a polarized source to exist there;
unverified.
Rubin/LSST, on a multi-year horizon. Dec −55.94 is inside WFD (−65 to +5), survey began
2026-06-29. Its 9.6 deg² field solves the area problem outright and its 3-day cadence is the
only realistic route to a lensed variable — which is the sole observable that breaks the
mass-sheet degeneracy. It cannot resolve Einstein crosses (0.7–0.8″ seeing vs 1–2″
crosses), so it complements JWST rather than replacing it.
NOT NEEDED — closed off
Gaia. Parallax at z = 0.296 (~1 Gpc) is ~1 nanoarcsecond against Gaia's ~20 μas floor —
four orders of magnitude short. Useful only for the astrometric reference frame and
foreground-star rejection. Not for cluster 3D structure.
More JWST filters for "polarization." JWST has no polarimetric mode in any instrument.
Ever. This is not a gap to be filled.
Ptychography from JWST dithers. Requires coherent illumination; astronomical sources are
mutually incoherent, so there is no phase to retrieve. §6 makes the
weak lensing is already a truncated ptychography, and the honest
extension is flexion (third shape moments) — which needs no new data, only a re-run of
extraction, and works in the weak regime.
3D mass from lensing alone. κ is a projection; any 3D distribution with the same
projection lenses identically. 3D requires multiple line-of-sight weightings (ρ from
lensing, n² from X-ray, nT from SZ) — all three of which are on disk. But the Bullet is
mid-merger, so equilibrium deprojection is invalid; its 3D orientation comes from shock
geometry instead.
Why the images could not be regenerated — and the fix
Six of the eight figures the README cited as results have no generating code anywhere in the
repository. They cannot be reproduced, cannot be checked against the nulls, and cannot be
updated when the data improves. That is why they survived refutation: there was nothing to
re-run that would have shown them changing.
Cody's diagnosis of the cause is correct and is adopted here: exploratory code was written
somewhere ephemeral and the output was kept while the code was lost. A persistent working
directory is the fix — text is negligible in size next to 250 GB of FITS, and a work
directory full of experimental engines is both provenance and a record of what had to be
learned. The model is Ptolemy2/working: experiment there, promote what works into the
codebase, never let the notepad pollute the product.
a figure with no committed generating script is not a
result. It is an illustration, and it goes under "Figures on disk" with that label.
What I got wrong in this session, plainly
Said MeerKAT radio data was unnecessary, then said it was integral. It is required.
§3 above is the resolved answer.
Proposed magnification bias without first checking the precondition. The catalog's median
flux sits almost on the detection limit, so the count-slope fit runs inside the
incompleteness regime and my α = 0.870 is unreliable.
Mapped "how many photons through a pixel" onto escape-time colouring, which is the wrong
quantity. Cody's own 2026-08-14 note already had it right — a density accumulation buffer
(Buddhabrot), with (x,y,t) so arrival time is carried.
Read the README's "Already Confirmed" list as results, when the 2026-08-14 nulls had
already refuted most of it. That is the failure this document exists to prevent recurring.
What Data, From Which Telescope, And What Each Is For
2026-08-17. Written against the claim as Cody restates it:
Spacetime vacuum is a medium. The shape of that compressible fluid is what we call
dark matter — not a stuff that alters curvature.
That reframing changes the data priorities, because a compressible medium has specific
observables (pressure, sound speed, shocks, equation of state) that a collisionless-stuff
hypothesis does not care about. Section 3 is the consequence and it is the most useful part
of this document.
THE RESOLUTION-CEILING RULE — applied first, to our own results
The Bruniquel Cave principle. C14 has a ceiling near 47–50 kyr. The cave's stalagmite
result came back at that ceiling — which means the ceiling was what was measured, not the
age. Switching to U-Th dating of the calcite regrowth gave 176,000 years: a questionable
result became a landmark one, purely by changing method rather than improving the old one.
a result that lands at the instrument's limit is a measurement OF the limit. It
requires a different method, not a better version of the same one.
Applied honestly to this repository, three results are limit-artifacts and one of them is
mine from today:
⚠ R2's empirical claim is resolution-limited — correcting it now
I reported that the Galactic Faraday foreground is common-mode across the transect, based on:
That is the C14 error exactly. The DM separation is below the map resolution, so I
could not have detected a gradient if one existed. And σ (19.669) exceeds the value
(18.274), so the foreground RM is not significantly different from zero at 1σ.
"the foreground is uniform across the transect."
"the foreground is unresolved at 6.87′. Uniformity is untested."
the reasoning that a common additive offset drags a ratio toward 1 (the
particle verdict). That is analytic and stands. What does not survive: the claim that the
foreground is common-mode here.
a high-density RM grid — POSSUM/ASKAP, or targeted
polarimetry — not a re-read of Hutschenreuter.
The other two
Planck SZ. MILCA y-map has 1.72′ pixels and a 10′ beam. It cannot resolve the
2.89′ DM separation. Any statement about pressure structure in the Bullet from this map is a
statement about the beam. Different instrument required: SPT or ACT.
MeerKAT radio null (N5). Already correctly self-flagged: 15″ = 67 kpc/beam against ~1 kpc
predicted structure — two orders too coarse. The null is about the beam, not the physics.
the magnification-bias count slope α = 0.870 was fit inside
the incompleteness regime (catalog median flux sits almost on the detection limit). Same
error class. A deeper external reference catalog is the different method.

Six telescope directories exist and are empty: SPT, ACT, ALMA, ATCA, VLA, MOST. Those are
the acquisition list, and they are not equally urgent — see below.
Organised by what each observable is FOR
The DM residual everyone actually wants:
Two of three are on disk. This is computable now at HST resolution, and it is the
literature-comparable quantity (Clowe+2006 used exactly this logic).
What the restated claim changes — and the test it makes available
If dark matter is the shape of a compressible medium rather than collisionless stuff, the
diagnostic observable is not mass, it is the equation of state. And that gives a sharp
test the repo has never run, using physics specific to this cluster:
Across a SHOCK, both density and pressure jump. Across a COLD FRONT, pressure is
continuous while density jumps.
The Bullet has both discontinuities — the bow shock (Mach ~3) and the bullet subcluster's
cold front. So density and pressure peaks are physically separated in this system, and that
separation is measurable rather than assumed.
The test:
This is falsifiable, it is not degenerate with the mass-sheet transformation (it compares
morphology, not normalisation), and it does not require polarization, a variable source, or
Einstein crosses. It requires three maps at matched resolution:
So the highest-value single acquisition is resolved SZ. Not MeerKAT Q/U. The Q/U blocks
the old RM-ratio test; resolved SZ enables a better test of the claim as now stated, with
two of three inputs already in hand.
Priority order, revised on that basis:
SPT-SZ or ACT y-map (~1′) — enables the P-vs-ρ-vs-κ test. Bullet is in the SPT
footprint. New top priority.
Rerun the pipeline on HST 10200 — zero acquisition; fixes the off-field cause of N1–N4.
XMM temperature map — completes P = nkT independently of SZ, and gives sound speed.
MeerKAT/ATCA/VLA Stokes Q/U — the RM-ratio test, which R2 shows also needs foreground
subtraction at better than 6.87′.
High-density RM grid (POSSUM/ASKAP) — the different method R2's correction demands.
Rotation curves — and Andromeda as the testbed
Rotation curves test the DM density profile, which is a shape statement, so they bear
directly on the restated claim rather than tangentially.
Gaia is genuinely useful here — and this is the reverse of the Bullet case, where I
correctly said it was useless. At Milky Way distances parallax works, so Gaia gives the
Galactic circular-velocity curve directly (Eilers+2019 and later work find a declining
curve out to ~25 kpc, which is itself a constraint on halo shape). That is a real DM-halo
measurement from data designed for it.
M31 as the working testbed is a good call, for reasons that are specific rather than
convenient:
Close and resolved — 785 kpc, so structure is resolvable in a way no other massive
spiral is.
Resolved multiple ways — HST PHAT (panchromatic stellar populations), HI rotation
curves (WSRT/GBT), Spitzer/Herschel dust and gas, JWST now, plus Gaia proper motion for its
3D velocity vector.
Not a nucleus problem — as Cody notes, EHT-scale physics is deferred; M31 tests halo
shape, which is the current question.
A known rotation curve to check any method against before pointing it at a cluster.
M31 is where a method can be *validated against a
known answer*, which is exactly what the Bullet cannot provide. Same role Ptolemy2/working
plays for code.
PTorrent — one downloader instead of N scripts
— seven overlapping downloaders, each with its own
state file and its own resume logic. That is the same provenance failure as the orphan images,
in a different register.
a single Linux console (curses) manager with
one state store, byte-range resume, pause-on-signal-loss already written
per-archive adapters (MAST, Chandra CDA, SARAO GraphQL, ASKAP/CASDA, NED/IRSA)
AWS S3 path for MAST where available (enableclouddataset, cloud_only=True) — the real
bulk-speed win, since these archives publish no torrents
a queue view, throughput, and a visible reason when something is paused rather than failed
Not built. Scoped here so it is a task rather than an aspiration.
Summary — what is necessary, and for what
Necessary and blocking nothing (do first, no acquisition):
rerun weak lensing on HST 10200; compute ΣDM = κ − Σgas − Σ_stars at HST resolution.
Necessary for the restated claim (top acquisition):
resolved SZ from SPT or ACT. Enables the κ-vs-P-vs-ρ morphology test, which is the
sharpest available test of "shape of a compressible medium" and needs no polarization.
XMM temperature map.
Necessary for the original RM-ratio prediction: real Stokes Q/U (MeerKAT/SARAO, or ATCA,
or VLA) plus a foreground map finer than 6.87′.
Necessary for method validation, not for the Bullet: Gaia (Milky Way rotation curve) and
M31 multi-wavelength as the testbed.
Not necessary / closed: Gaia for Bullet distances; any JWST filter for polarization (no
polarimetric mode exists); ptychography from incoherent astronomical dithers.
BulletCluster — Actual Results
Audited 2026-08-17. Every item on this page is a measurement on real observational
data, with code in the repo that reproduces it, and its limits stated.
Nothing here comes from radio/meerkat/synthetic/. Nothing here is a demonstration that a
method runs. What was removed, and why, is in .
one data product, one methodological finding, one measurement, five nulls, one
negative control, two infrastructure fixes. All of it real. None of it confirms the
Abrikosov hypothesis, and none of it refutes it either.
R1 — Chandra X-ray mosaic [DATA PRODUCT]
Bow shock and cold front cleanly resolved. Built by .
Limits, stated in the code: exposure-weighted counts, not surface brightness. No
exposure map, no vignetting correction, no background subtraction, no point-source removal.
Adequate for morphology and correlation. NOT for photometry, temperature, or flux.
CIAO merge_obs/fluximage required if flux is ever needed.
This is the single most solid thing in the repository.
R2 — The RM-ratio test is biased toward its own null hypothesis [METHODOLOGICAL, and the most important result here]
Hutschenreuter et al. 2022 Galactic Faraday sky (D4/D6), Planck 353/217 GHz I/Q/U
The engine's whole prediction is RM(DM)/RM(gas) against a threshold of 0.95. Both terms
sit behind the same Milky Way Faraday screen, and the screen was assumed to cancel in the
ratio. It does not:
A common additive foreground does not cancel in a ratio — it drags the ratio
toward 1, which is the particle verdict. The test is biased toward the answer it was
built to refute.
Measured, at the Bullet sightline (l = 266.019, b = −21.257):
All five reference points — DMNW, DMSE, GASNW, GASSE, CENTROID — fall in ONE HEALPix
pixel (2142697). The Galactic Faraday map at nside 512 cannot resolve the DM separation
at all.
⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-17 — the resolution ceiling. An earlier version of this entry
claimed the foreground is common-mode across the transect. That was a limit artifact.
The DM separation (2.891′) is below the map pixel (6.871′), so a gradient could not have
been detected if one existed; and σ (19.669) exceeds the value (18.274), so the
foreground RM is not significantly different from zero at 1σ.
"the foreground is uniform across the transect."
"the foreground is unresolved at 6.87′. Uniformity is untested."
What stands, because it is analytic rather than measured: a common additive offset does
not cancel in a ratio — it drags the ratio toward 1, the particle verdict. Cluster ICM
rotation measures run 1e1–1e3 rad/m², so at the low end an ~18 rad/m² offset is comparable to
the signal. So Q/U acquisition remains necessary-but-insufficient, and the reason is now
the foreground must be resolved, not merely estimated.
Different method required, not a better version of this one: a high-density RM grid
(POSSUM/ASKAP, or targeted polarimetry). See §0 for why re-reading
Hutschenreuter cannot settle it.
acquiring real Stokes Q/U is necessary but NOT sufficient. The foreground
has to be subtracted before the 0.95 threshold means anything. That requirement did not
exist in the project plan before this script ran.
A sanity check that also passed, worth keeping: HEALPix RING ordering verified by
mean |RM| in the Galactic plane (187.4) vs the polar cap (4.1) — the correct sign and
magnitude, so the ordering assumption is not silently wrong.
R3 — Radio halo spectral index and power spectrum [MEASUREMENT + NULL]
real MeerKAT MGCLS L-band, 10 planes, 996.6–1656.2 MHz
radio/bulletspectralindex.fits
No preferred scale. No standing-wave surface.
Limits, both recorded in the code: the slope is shallower than Kolmogorov (−3.67), so
noise contributes to it; and 15″ = 67 kpc/beam while the predicted fuzzy-DM structure is
~1 kpc — two orders of magnitude too coarse to reach the predicted scale. This test
cannot reach the thing it was aimed at, so the null is weak evidence about the hypothesis
and strong evidence about the instrument.
R4 — κ is noise-dominated [NULL]
. Lensing produces E-mode only; B-mode (shear rotated 45°)
carries no lensing signal by construction, so E/B is the null.
The pipeline reproduces the shipped kappa.npy to 1.11e-16 — this is the same map, not
a reimplementation, so the null applies to every product derived from it.
The blob field is smoothed shape noise. This does not refute wave DM; it says this map
cannot test it.
R5 — ψ is integrated noise; the smooth gradient is the operator [NULL]
. psik = -2 kappak / k^2 — the 1/k² is a brutal
low-pass that manufactures a large-scale gradient from any input.
89% of ψ's power sits in three wavenumbers. A smooth large-scale gradient in ψ is
guaranteed by the operator and is not evidence of anything.
This null is what retires the "gradient" imagery. See .
R6 — Emission does not track L_(I|O) [NULL]
All |z| < 2 against a circular-shift null, and E and B agree throughout:
The visual agreement between the ptychography composite and L_(I|O) is not present as a
correlation. Two maps dominated by one large-scale mode look aligned regardless of
content. That the B-mode tracks as well as the E-mode is the tell.
R7 — Shape test inconclusive, with an identified cause [DIAGNOSTIC]
. Does the gradient track the real X-ray gas or the NFW
model placed at DMNW/DMSE? Those are spatially separated, so they are distinguishable.
The reference mosaic is one tile, 5.66′ × 2.51′. The test was asked to find a halo that
is not in the image.
R4–R7 are one disease, not four failures: single-tile footprint, DM_NW off-field, too
few background galaxies. κ noisy → ψ integrated noise → every correlation meaningless.
Pre-registered thresholds for the re-run (scripts rerun unchanged, no tuning):
psiE/psiB >> 1 (now 0.724) and kappa E/B >> 1 (now 1.023). Only then are strong-lensing
steps worth attempting.
R8 — The hand-drawn constraint never entered the pipeline [NEGATIVE CONTROL, PASSED]
TheBulletCluster-defined.png is a hand-annotated constraint band. Verified by grep:
no code reads it. It cannot have leaked into any output. This is a real control and it
passed — worth keeping precisely because the failure mode it guards against is severe.
R9 — Download infrastructure [ENGINEERING]
Two real faults found and fixed, both in :
Observations.getproductlist() on all 292 observations at once hung ~7 hours at 0%
CPU with zero files written — astroquery puts no timeout on the call. Now batched
(15/call) with retry and per-batch logging, so a stall is visible immediately.
The product filter was endswith((".fits", "drz.fits", "cal.fits", "_i2d.fits")) — a
bare ".fits" subsumes every other pattern, so the mask did nothing: 43,326 products
passed (~118 MB each, terabytes) instead of the intended ~14 GB.
— pauses on signal loss rather than aborting, so a network
switch costs one TCP handshake instead of a full re-query.
What all of this does and does not support
that the Chandra morphology is solid; that the current κ map cannot test the
hypothesis and the reason is field size; that the central RM-ratio test has a
previously-unquantified bias toward the particle verdict.
any claim about wave vs particle dark matter. The zero-free-parameter
prediction has never been run on observational data, because the data it needs does not
exist on disk.
Does not refute the hypothesis either. Every null here is a null about an instrument
or a footprint, not about the physics. R3 and R4 both say so explicitly.
Retracted Claims — recorded here, excised from the live files
2026-08-17. This is the permanent record. Each item is preserved with its original
wording and the reason it fails, so nothing is lost — and then removed from
and the viewer, rather than annotated in place.
Why removal rather than annotation
The 2026-08-14 addendum in diagnosed most of this correctly. It then said:
"Addenda, not corrections. Every prior result stands as written*; these sit beneath
them."*
That policy is the actual fault, and it cost real time. A refuted claim left in a file is
still read as a claim — by a human skimming, and by any automated reader that ingests the
directory. "Noted as wrong" is not the same as "not present." Anything still in the file is
still in context.
recorded once, here. Removed there.

L_(I|O) — Formal Specification
Written 2026-08-14. Each apparatus, its prerequisites, and its regime of validity.
The purpose of this document is to state what L_(I|O) is, what each step
requires, and where each step stops being valid — so that a result is
never read out of a step whose preconditions were not met. Every null recorded
in this repo on 2026-08-14 was a step run outside its regime.
The identification
L_(I|O) is the Fermat potential. Not analogously — the same expression.
with
symbol . meaning
`theta` . image position — where you see it
`beta` . source position — where it actually is
`psi` . lensing potential (the aberration function)
`alpha = grad psi` . deflection angle
`kappa = ½ grad² psi` . convergence (projected surface density / Sigma_crit)
The lens equation is beta = theta − alpha(theta), and images form where
grad_theta t = 0 — the stationary points, not the minima.
Consequences that follow immediately
An Einstein cross is L_(I|O)'s stationary set, made visible.
Time delays are the values of L_(I|O) at those points.
Image parities (minimum / saddle / maximum) are the catastrophe
nmin − nsaddle + n_max = 1, so a "4-image" cross is
really 5, one heavily demagnified near the centre.
The photon does not seek less-dense space. Saddle and maximum images
traverse the compressed region and arrive later (geometric + Shapiro delay).
The minimum image is the one that skirts it.
It is an aberration expansion — the same one as eyeglasses
The entire tensor content is one symmetric 2×2 matrix of second derivatives:
Split a Hessian into trace plus trace-free part. That is the same operation
as decomposing a stress tensor into isotropic pressure + deviatoric shear. No
transformation laws, no Christoffel symbols, no covariant derivatives are
required to use this. GR is needed to derive alpha = 2∫grad⊥Phi dl / c²;
it is not needed to apply it.
Adaptive optics is the inverse operation. Measure the aberration, apply its
conjugate. In lensing that is de-lensing — recover beta from the bent path.
AO gets a laser guide star as its reference; lensing has no reference unless a
multiply-imaged source supplies one.
⚠ Conjugation is not cancellation. ANC emits −p(t) and destroys energy.
AO emits e^(−i·phi) and redirects it — same photons, reorganised into a
focus. The Monad's purpose (wide beam → point) is conjugation.
The pipeline, step by step, with prerequisites
# . step . requires . regime . status here
1 . shear `gamma` from galaxy shapes . background galaxies, 2nd shape moments . weak . **done** (noisy)
2 . Kaiser–Squires → `kappa` . step 1; `kappa << 1` . weak . **done** — E/B = 1.023
3 . `psi = grad⁻²(2 kappa)` . step 2 . weak . **done** — integrated noise
3b . **FLEXION `F`, `G`** . **3rd shape moments** . weak . **NOT COMPUTED — no data**
4 . `alpha = grad psi` . step 3 . weak . **done**
5 . Fermat `phi = ½\ . theta−beta\ . ² − psi` . **a source position `beta`** . either . **unavailable**
6 . arrival time `t ∝ phi` . step 5 . either . **unavailable**
7 . images at `grad phi = 0` . identified multiple images . strong . **unavailable**
8 . magnification `mu = 1/det A` . `kappa ~ 1` . **strong** . **unavailable**
9 . critical curves at `det A = 0` . `kappa ~ 1` . **strong** . **unavailable**
Steps 1–4 are weak lensing. Steps 5–9 are strong lensing. The current
implementation stops at step 4.
⚠ Regime boundaries that must be checked before reading a result
Caustics require kappa ~ 1.
kappa_rms = 0.072, so det A ≈ 1 everywhere and 1 − kappa
never approaches zero. There are no caustics in a weak-lensing map, by
construction. Not faint — absent from this kind of data.
psi amplifies noise catastrophically.
The 1/k² is a brutal low-pass. Noise in kappa is roughly flat in k, so
psi is dominated by the lowest wavenumbers whatever the input. Measured:
89% of psi_E's power sits in the 3 lowest wavenumbers (kappa: 13%).
A smooth large-scale gradient in psi is guaranteed by the operator and is
not evidence of signal.
kappa, psi and alpha are the same field, differently filtered.
alpha and psi contain no information absent from kappa. "Did the
gradient show the mass or the path?" is not a well-posed question — the path is
a deterministic functional of the mass.
Mandatory nulls
No result from this pipeline is reportable without its null.
test . null . why
any `kappa` structure . **B-mode** (shear rotated 45°) . lensing produces E-mode ONLY; B is systematics + noise
any map–map correlation . **circular shift** of one map . both fields are autocorrelated; textbook p-values are meaningless
any spectral feature . **power-law fit + residual scatter** . turbulence is a power law; interference is a *peak*
a hand-drawn region . **check no code reads it** . verified by grep for `The_Bullet_Cluster-defined.png` — nothing does
Read the z-score, never the raw r.
Measured state, 2026-08-14
Cause, single and shared: the reference mosaic is one tile
(jw04598-o001t001), a 5.66′ × 2.51′ strip. **DMNW — the main cluster's mass
peak — falls outside the field (px y = 84.8 against ny = 78). DM_SE sits 12 px
from the bottom edge. Too little area, too few background galaxies.
Four symptoms, one disease. Not four independent failures.
Pre-registered thresholds for the re-run
When the full 292-observation mosaic completes, rerun unchanged. A real
reconstruction must show:
psiE / psiB well above 1 (currently 0.724)
kappa E/B well above 1 (currently 1.023)
and only then are steps 5–9 worth attempting
What each intended use actually needs
you want . you need . have it?
the mass map . steps 1–2 . yes, noisy
the aberration map . steps 3–4 — **this is `psi`/`alpha`, NOT the RGB composite** . yes, noise
focusing / coma structure . **step 3b, flexion** — 3rd shape moments . **no — `source_extract.py` keeps only E1/E2**
caustics, focal points . steps 8–9, `kappa ~ 1` . no — needs strong lensing
"through what space did the photon travel" . steps 5–7, a source position . no — needs multiple images
time delays / path-integral differences . steps 5–6 . no — needs a multiply-imaged **variable** source
The Einstein crosses are not an enhancement. They are the only route to
steps 5–9, because they supply the beta that 5–7 require and the kappa ~ 1
that 8–9 require — and the source becomes its own reference, removing the
observer's choice of where to look.
Ptychography — what the word does and does not mean here
Real ptychography maps the aberration. Iterative reconstruction (ePIE and
descendants) solves simultaneously for the object and the probe — and probe
retrieval yields the illuminating wavefront, i.e. the aberration function. This
is routinely used to characterise X-ray optics.
does not do this. It is an RGB composite of
F444W/F356W/F277W: three intensity images, no coherent probe, no overlapping
scan, no phase retrieval, no phase at all. It maps emission — where the
galaxies are. Interference is a phase phenomenon and astronomical sources are
mutually incoherent, so no interference pattern can appear in it.
But weak lensing is already structurally ptychographic. Every background
galaxy samples the lens potential at a different position: many overlapping
probes, one aberration function, solved jointly. The difference is truncation —
Weak lensing is a truncated ptychography. Adding flexion extends the
reconstruction by one Zernike order using data already present in the images —
and unlike caustics, flexion works in the weak regime, so it does not have to
wait for kappa ~ 1.

The Ainulindalë Conjecture — Abrikosov Lattice / σ=½ ZD boundary hypothesis
Engine verified on synthetic data. Real MeerKAT Q/U data pending. JWST mosaic pending.
The Central Claim
Dark matter is not a particle. It is the Abrikosov vortex lattice of the prime number condensate — the same structure Alexei Abrikosov described in Type II superconductors in 1957 (Nobel Prize in Physics, 2003), instantiated in the superconducting medium of space.
The Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-558) is conventionally cited as the strongest evidence for particle dark matter. This repository makes the opposite argument: the Bullet Cluster is a Meissner-Abrikosov phase separation event — a collision that separated the superconducting condensate (baryonic gas, electromagnetically coupled) from the Abrikosov vortex lattice (dark matter, topologically pinned, electromagnetically decoupled).
The vortex passes through without scattering because it IS the zero of the condensate field — |Ψ| = 0 at the vortex core — and there is nothing for electromagnetic radiation to scatter against. It gravitates because it carries energy-momentum. Lensing sees it. X-rays don't.
The Testable Prediction
Zero free parameters. Threshold set before looking at real Q/U data.
NEVER RUN ON OBSERVATIONAL DATA.
The engine has only ever been run on synthetic cubes from ,
which injects ΔRM at the DM peaks and then recovers it (wave 0.861 / particle 0.967).
That is a correct harness self-test and it is circular by construction — it verifies the
code, not the universe. It is not a result. See RT4.
Two things block the real test, not one:
Real Stokes Q/U — MGCLS DR1 has Stokes I only (NAXIS4 = 1, verified on the files).
Foreground subtraction — the Galactic Faraday screen is common-mode and additive
(18.27 ± 19.67 rad/m², all reference points in ONE HEALPix pixel), which drags a ratio
the particle verdict. Acquiring Q/U is necessary but not sufficient.
See R2.

Einstein Cross data catalog — ptychography / L_(I|O) / polarization
Written 2026-08-18. A REQUIREMENTS CHECKLIST, not an inventory. Nothing here
claims a dataset exists until the verified column says so against an archive
query. Rows marked MAY NOT EXIST are flagged because the physics says the
observation is probably impossible, not because nobody looked.
PROVENANCE RULE. Every number produced from this data carries its class in
SYNTHETIC tests the code, CALIBRATION tests the pipeline,
RESULT tests the hypothesis. Never report the first two as results.
The five targets
key . object . z_lens . z_src . scale . why it is in the set
A1 . MACS J1149.5+2223 (SN Refsdal) . 0.544 . 1.49 . cluster . the reappearance SX was PREDICTED from lens models — the only prospective test in the set
A2 . SDSS J1004+4112 . 0.68 . 1.734 . cluster . ~15" separation, long measured delays; bridges cluster and galaxy scale
A3 . RX J1131−1231 . 0.295 . 0.658 . galaxy . best-characterised Fermat potential, long delays
A4 . HE 0435−1223 . 0.454 . 1.689 . galaxy . independent system — exists so A3 cannot be a fluke
A5 . Q2237+0305 (Huchra's Lens) . 0.0394 . 1.695 . galaxy . the original Einstein Cross. Delays are HOURS, so useless for dt — the cleanest pure-geometry case
PTYCHOGRAPHY — and the current download is the wrong product
Ptychography reconstructs phase from overlapping intensity measurements with
known probe positions. Astronomically that means many dithered exposures
plus a PSF model. It does not work from a mosaic.
THE DOWNLOAD SCRIPT IS FETCHING THE WRONG FILES FOR THIS. Its own banner
reads *"products: drizzled mosaics only ('i2d.fits', 'drz.fits',
'_drc.fits')"*. Drizzling RESAMPLES and COMBINES the dithers — it destroys
exactly the per-exposure sub-pixel offsets ptychography needs. The 190 GB
already downloaded is the right targets in the wrong product class.
--all-products.
need . product . instrument . notes
individual dithered frames . `_flt`, `_flc` . HST ACS/WFC3/WFPC2 . flat-fielded, NOT drizzled. `_flc` = CTE-corrected
individual dithered frames . `_cal`, `_rate` . JWST NIRCam/MIRI . stage-2 per-exposure
dither pattern / WCS . headers of the above . — . the "probe positions". Must be sub-pixel accurate
PSF model (the probe) . TinyTim / WebbPSF . — . generated, not downloaded. **CALIBRATION**
pixel-area / distortion maps . IDCTAB, `_npl` . — . needed before any position is trusted
read noise / gain . instrument handbook . — . sets the noise floor of the phase retrieval
≥ 4 dithered exposures in one filter with
sub-pixel offsets, plus a PSF model at the field position. More filters buys
chromatic phase; more epochs buys microlensing separation.
L_(I|O) PHOTON PATH — mostly catalogue, not imaging
The Fermat potential difference is what L_(I|O) − L is:
dt ≈ D[(θ−β)²/2 − ψ(θ)]. To evaluate it per target you need:
need . source . verified
image positions θ (4 images, milliarcsec) . HST astrometry / VLBI where radio-loud . ☐
measured time delays Δt . COSMOGRAIL, H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO published curves . ☐
lens redshift z_l, source redshift z_s . spectroscopy (published) . ☐
lens light profile / ellipticity . HST imaging, already have . ☐
line-of-sight convergence κ_ext . weak-lensing + number counts . ☐
stellar velocity dispersion σ_v . Keck/VLT spectroscopy . ☐
**published lens model to run FORWARD against** . TDCOSMO data releases . ☐
Caveat from the download script, kept because it is load-bearing: a quad
lens is the STRONG regime (κ ~ 1). Kaiser–Squires is a linear inversion valid
for κ ≪ 1. Do not feed these to boundedlensingpipeline() and expect
meaning — run the ψ → α → β chain FORWARD on a published model instead.
A5 has delays of HOURS. It cannot test dt. It is in the set for geometry only.
POLARIZATION VECTOR FIELD — and where it does not exist
Needs Stokes I, Q, U at minimum; V for circular.
band . instrument . product . status
radio . VLA / VLBA full-Stokes . `.ms`, Q/U cubes . **MAY NOT EXIST** — A3/A4/A5 are radio-QUIET quasars. Check NVSS/FIRST/VLASS first; expect non-detections
radio . MERLIN / EVN . — . only if the source is radio-loud
mm . ALMA full-pol . Band 3–7 Q/U . check ALMA archive per target
optical . HST ACS/WFC POL0V, POL60V, POL120V . `_flt` per polarizer . the workhorse. Needs all three angles
optical . HST WFPC2 POLQ . — . older, A5 has WFPC2 coverage
optical . VLT FORS2 imaging polarimetry . — . ground, seeing-limited
NIR . HST NICMOS POL0S/POL120S/POL240S . — . if NIR polarimetry is wanted
X-ray . IXPE . — . **ALMOST CERTAINLY IMPOSSIBLE.** IXPE needs bright sources; these quasars are orders of magnitude too faint. Do not budget for it
X-ray . Chandra / XMM . I only . **no polarimetry** — imaging and spectra only
a full radio-through-X-ray polarization vector
field for all five targets is very likely not obtainable from existing
archives. The realistic product is HST optical polarimetry where it exists,
plus radio Q/U for whichever target turns out to be radio-loud. State that
before promising a vector field.
Supporting, all bands
need . why
Galactic extinction map (SFD/Planck) . de-redden before any colour or polarization angle
Galactic foreground polarization (Planck 353 GHz) . **subtract it** — otherwise the foreground IS your signal. Already on disk: `mm_sz/planck`
Faraday rotation map . radio polarization angle is meaningless without RM
PSF stars in-field . empirical PSF check against TinyTim/WebbPSF
microlensing light curves (OGLE/COSMOGRAIL) . A5 especially — microlensing corrupts flux ratios
The checklist, per target
Copy this block per target and fill it in. Nothing is a RESULT until the
control column is also filled.
What to do next, in order
Re-run the download with --all-products for group A. The drizzled
mosaics already on disk stay useful for astrometry; the per-exposure frames
are what ptychography needs and are not yet present.
Query, do not assume. Before adding a polarization row to any target,
query the archive. Sections 3's "MAY NOT EXIST" rows exist so a negative is
recorded as a negative rather than as a gap.
Forward-model first. Run ψ → α → β on a published lens model and check it
reproduces the measured image positions. That is CALIBRATION. Only after it
closes does anything computed from our own reconstruction become a RESULT.

§1 — The Algebraic Claim
Euler's formula, e^{iθ} = cos(θ) + i·sin(θ), is not new to this framework — it is
already the literal basis of 's Dirichlet projection: the cosine channel
drives J_red ( 's "real, un-shakeable" side, the persistent
projection), the sine channel drives J_blue (Laurelin's "shakeable" side, the
projection that vanishes on the natural lattice θ = 0, π, 2π, ...). This paper
asks a narrower, testable question: what happens when the 16 sedenion basis
directions — already fixed by 's spoke_angle(k) = 2πk/16 − π/2, using
only THEANGLE = π/8 established in — are read as the 16th
roots of unity and summed one at a time?
Define the Axis N-shape spiral:
Claim, verified exactly (zero free parameters, THE_ANGLE only):
The partial-sum spiral's phase crosses the real axis — Telperion's axis, the
cos(θ) term of Euler's formula, with zero Laurelin (sin) component — at
exactly m = 8, the halfway index. 8/16 = 1/2. This is not fit; it is the
elementary trigonometric fact that the resultant of a symmetric arc of unit
vectors has phase equal to the angular midpoint of the arc summed so far, applied
to the specific arc THE_ANGLE already fixes. The crossing is unique — no other
index among the 16 crosses the real axis (verified computationally, see §3).
§2 — What Was Tried First, and Failed
The original hypothesis, stated plainly and kept in the record rather than
that |S_m| (the partial-sum magnitude) would have a local
minimum at m=8, mirroring the N-shape's single ADE-A₂ fold crossing
This is false. |S_m| is near its maximum at m=7–8 (the central lobe of the
Dirichlet kernel) and returns to zero only at m=15 — the trivial, complete sum
of all 16 roots of unity, the elementary identity Σ_{k=0}^{15} e^{2πik/16} = 0.
That identity is real but says nothing new: it is the "whole coin" cancelling
exactly, the same fact wiki/53 uses to argue against half-coin cryptographic
hardness assumptions, here appearing as pure root-of-unity arithmetic.
The real structure was not in the magnitude. It was in the phase, and it was not
the structure that was being looked for. Recorded per the repository's own
Scientific Integrity convention ( , 's
"Failed predictions stay in the record. Period. Full stop.") — extended here to
a sibling repository under the same discipline.

Fourth Age Paper. One Paper. One Claim. One Engine. One Wiki.
The Claim
The Cayley–Dickson doubling boundary is a chiral mirror,
whose exactly two fixed points — e0 and e(dim/2) — are precisely the indices
belonging to no zero-divisor plane, at every level from dim = 16 upward.
compute the orphans at any higher level. If they are not [0, dim/2],

STANDS. Verified by enumeration at dim = 16, 32, 64, and at dim = 128

The productive failure

A zero divisor confined to one half has nullity an even multiple of 4.
A zero divisor spanning the boundary has nullity an odd multiple of 4.
P6 — CONFIRMED (2026-08-15, after the paper was written). The parity law holds at

Both match the closed form ZD(d) = d(d + 3/2 − 3·log₂d) − 4 to the unit, and
lower(2d) = upper(2d) = total(d) exactly. The main claim's orphans hold at both levels
too.

Why it is a lever
The mirror's two fixed points are the identity e_0 (which generates the boundary and
does not live on it — [e0,·,·] = 0) and e(dim/2), the generator introduced by that
doubling. They pair with nothing, they sit in no Assessor, and they carry no force —
the subspace 0_RB calls gravity, present as absence.
A fulcrum does no work. Everything else balances across them in equal number:
And because the mirror is chiral, successive boundaries do not stack into parallel
reflections. Two reflections compose to a rotation, and the boundaries sit at dim/2 —
constant step in log2, constant pitch ln 2. Rotation plus constant logarithmic
the Archimedes screw of Phase 24, reached from the algebra
rather than from the primes.

Collatz as the 2-adic Shift
Fourth Age Paper. One Paper. One Result. One Engine. One Wiki.
The departure from the template
Every other Fourth Age paper is One Paper, One Claim. This one has no claim
and no prediction, and there is no .
That is the protocol applied, not relaxed. Pre-registration is a device for
stopping yourself reinterpreting a result after seeing it, and it means something
only when the outcome is genuinely unknown at registration. Everything measured
here is either a theorem already in the literature or an exact enumeration over a
finite space. There is nothing to be wrong about, so there is nothing to
pre-register.
What replaces the claim is a provenance label on every result, printed by the
KNOWN with an attribution, or OURS.
Nothing borrowed is allowed to read as ours.
The Result
The Collatz map is the one-sided binary shift on Z₂, under an explicit
measure-preserving change of coordinates — the parity vector. Its pieces are
affine on residue classes mod 2^k; its branch tree is Pascal's triangle
exactly; its cycles are rationals with denominator 2^k − 3^d.
T = ADD ∘ SCALE ∘ SIGN. No new
generator is required.
The map used throughout is the shortcut map, one halving folded into the odd
branch so every step does work:
What this means for the conjecture — and what it does not
The dynamics of the shift are completely understood: entropy log 2, dense
periodic points, uncountably many orbits. Total chaos, fully solved. The Collatz
conjecture asserts that N — dense in Z₂ and of measure zero — misses all of
it. So the difficulty is not in the map. It is in how two incompatible metrics,
the 2-adic and the archimedean, fail to see each other.
Nothing in this paper proves the conjecture, disproves it, or is evidence
either way. Stated plainly so it cannot be read otherwise.

1, which truncates the low tail. It is not corrected for and not hidden.
The direction result — OURS
direction . what happens . rate
**down** (forward `T`) . exactly 2-to-1; one parity bit destroyed per step; provenance discarded . `log 2` nats/step
**up** (backward tree on `N`) . mean out-degree `4/3`; enumerates possibilities, propagates nothing . `log(4/3)` nats/step
**shortfall** . `log(3/2)`, **exactly**
Going up the tower does not propagate information — it enumerates. Going down
does, and what propagates is the address. The gap between the two directions is
log(3/2), the odd branch's own gain: the arithmetic the 2-adic metric cannot
see, priced per step.

and SCALE have different identities (0 and 1); the +1 is the only thing

The three faults on the first run — all mine, none the mathematics
Kept on the record because they are the most useful part of the paper.
relation . diagnosis
`cycle_denominator` . necklace filter kept rotation-minimal words but not **primitive** ones, so `1010`, `101010`, … came through and one loop was reported as seven cycles

Collatz as the 2-adic Shift
2026-08-21. Cody, out of a run of pathway-mathematics reading:
*"multiple inputs to one small ordered loop… Collatz Conjecture… I see a
recursive decomposition on a modular function… what actually is it"*
The observation is correct, the object has a name, and this page says what it is.
analysis result. No claim, no prediction. Every result carries a
provenance label. See for the scorecard
and for the measurements.
The map, and the address
The shortcut map, one halving folded into the odd branch so every step does
work:
Record the even/odd decision at each step and you get the parity word — a
sequence of bits. That word is not a summary of the orbit. It is a coordinate:
the 2-adic address of n, and the orbit is what you get by reading the address
from the left.
Measured, exhaustively to k = 16 (65536 of 65536, no sampling):
Z/2^k → Z/2^k, n ↦ its first k parities, is a bijection, and
Q(T(n)) = shift(Q(n)).
The Collatz map is the one-sided binary shift. Not analogous to it —
conjugate to it, by a measure-preserving homeomorphism. This is Bernstein (1994)
and Bernstein–Lagarias (1996); the engine re-measures it rather than citing it.
The recursive decomposition on a modular function — named
T^k restricted to a residue class mod 2^k is an affine map:
with d = the number of odd steps, and d depending only on the class, never
on n. There are 2^k such pieces; refining k → k+1 splits every branch in
two.
That is the whole structure Cody was seeing. The "modular function" is the
indexing of the pieces by Z/2^k; the "recursive decomposition" is the
refinement. It is an iterated function system whose address space is the parity
word.
Verified for every class at every k ≤ 8 — 510 classes, slope 3^d/2^k in all of
them.
The tessellation — why the chaos is apparent
The intuition Cody arrived at from Hilbert, Koch and dragon curves — *"they seem
chaotic but are just tessellated"* — is exactly right here, and it is measurable.
Count, over the 2^k classes mod 2^k, how many odd steps each one takes:
That is C(8,d). Exact binomial at every k up to 12, with no error term.
The branch structure of the Collatz tree is Pascal's triangle — the most
ordered combinatorial object there is — read through a metric that scrambles it.
A dragon curve is a paperfolding sequence read off binary digits; a Hilbert curve
is a base-4 address; the Collatz orbit is a base-2 address. Same category of
a p-adic address rendered in the archimedean metric, which is what makes
it look like chaos.
And the second half of Cody's intuition — *"chaos in multiple dimensions becomes
order, which we see in the normal curve"* — follows from the first half as a
theorem rather than as an observation. log n along an orbit is a sum of k iid
log-steps whose count is Binomial(k, ½), so its limit is Gaussian by de
Moivre–Laplace. Measured at k = 20: `sup|binomial CDF − normal CDF| =
0.00139`, exact binomial, no sampling. The normal curve here is not an empirical
finding about Collatz. It is R4 in the limit.
The cycles, and the "near miss"
Every periodic parity word of length k with d ones determines exactly one
rational cycle, and its denominator is always 2^k − 3^d:
word . k . d . `2^k − 3^d` . x
`10` . 2 . 1 . **1** . **1**
`11` . 2 . 2 . −5 . −1
`100` . 3 . 1 . 5 . 1/5
`11000` . 5 . 2 . 23 . 5/23
`1101000` . 7 . 3 . 101 . 23/101
A cycle is an integer cycle only when 2^k − 3^d divides the numerator, and
2^k − 3^d = 1 happens at (k,d) = (2,1) and nowhere else (Levi ben Gerson /
Catalan, cited not proved). That single fact is why 1 → 2 → 1 is the
exceptional loop. Every other parity word gives a perfectly good cycle that
simply does not land in Z.
Enumerating primitive necklaces to k = 16: exactly one positive-integer
The candidate shapes are the continued-fraction convergents of
log₂3 = 1.58496250:
On the word "near miss"
This ladder is a linear form in logarithms: how close k·log2 can come to
d·log3 without equalling it. That is the same family as the Fermat
near-miss work (FourthAgePapers/FermatMonster,
) — in both cases the question is how
closely towers of small primes can approach one another without touching.
It is not the same problem, and it is not the Riemann Hypothesis. What RH
and this share is only the underlying arena: a lattice generated by logarithms of
small primes, and how well it approximates a target. Recorded as a family
resemblance so that it does not get promoted to an identity later.
The direction result — up the tower vs down it
Cody, same session:
*"going up the tower (reals to sedenion) is not information propagation; going
down the tower (sedenion to real numbers) is information propagation"*
In this system that is measurable, and it comes out clean.
Down — the forward map. T is well defined as Z/2^k → Z/2^(k-1), and every
fibre has exactly 2 elements, at every level, with no exceptional fibre. So
each forward step destroys exactly one bit: log 2 nats. The destroyed bit
never returns — provenance is discarded, exactly as discards
it on collection.
Up — the backward tree. n always has the predecessor 2n, and has an odd
predecessor iff n ≡ 2 (mod 3), a density-1/3 set. Mean out-degree measured
over n < 10⁶: 4/3, not 2.
The shortfall between the two directions is log(3/2) exactly — the odd
branch's own gain. Going up enumerates possibilities and propagates nothing;
going down propagates, and what propagates is the address. The gap is the
arithmetic the 2-adic metric cannot see, priced per step.
⚠ Correction kept on the record. The odd-predecessor condition is usually
written "n ≡ 2 (mod 3) and (2n−1)/3 is odd". The second half is
vacuous — 2n−1 is odd and 3 is odd, so the quotient is odd whenever it
is an integer at all. The first run of the engine predicted 7/6 from that
phantom condition and returned MATHS-FAULT. The engine now measures the
vacuity instead of assuming it, the density is exactly 1/3, and the shortfall
comes out exact. The fault improved the result.
Why σ = ½ is not a metaphor here
The shift is Bernoulli(½,½) under Haar measure, and the conjugacy of §1
preserves that measure. So half the steps are ×½ and half are ×3/2, and
the per-step geometric mean is √3/2 = 0.866 < 1.
The residual +0.0047 is termination bias — the sample stops at 1, which
truncates the low tail. Stated, not corrected for, not hidden.
The critical parity fraction where the drift vanishes is log2/log3 = 0.630930.
The system contracts because the two branches are balanced, and ½ sits below
the critical value with margin. Same shape as the reading of ∅_RB in
.clauderccanonicalmaths: self-adjointness is downstream of Jred = Jblue,
not assumed alongside it. Here the contraction is downstream of the balance.
The lineage verdict
Decomposed against the generational-lineage operation domain:
No new generator required. T is the smallest non-trivial composition using
all three tier-0 irreducibles at once — and that is exactly why it is hard. ADD
and SCALE have different identities (0 and 1), and the +1 is the only
n → 3n/2^v is a pure SCALE tower,
strictly ×3 forever, with no conjecture in it.
No section-5 emergence signature fires. The one that came closest — *a fixed set
of the wrong dimension* — resolves: the fixed points of T in Z are {0, −1},
the two constant parity words, and on N the attractor can only be a loop,
because every positive integer's word must alternate. Cody's *"one small
ordered loop"* is forced, not incidental.
Where the framework speaks — and one place it does not
— set the GC root to {1}. The Collatz conjecture is
then the collector's completeness claim: run it on N and it collects
nothing; the kernel is empty. And the descent is monotone in exactly the
designed sense — one parity bit consumed per step, never restored.
— the mod-3 leaves are the ORPHAN regime, with one
difference the instrument does not currently model: a sieve orphan at N is
adopted at 2N (bounded by universe size); a Collatz orphan is never
adopted (bounded algebraically). Two kinds of orphan.
L_(I|O) — forward is deterministic and free; backward is a branching tree
gated by a mod 3 test. Forward throws away one bit per step, backward must
guess it. The parity word is the private key — the same shape as *speaking
English is easy, the inverse is factoring the modulus*.
0_RB = e₀ — the attractor is the identity. "Every trajectory falls into
the identity" is the conjecture in this project's vocabulary.
⚠ The Two Trees do NOT split even/odd
Telperion = prime, Laurelin = composite. Even/odd is divisibility by 2, not
2 is prime and even, 9 is composite and odd. The tempting
mapping is wrong and is written down here as wrong so it does not get made
later.
The defensible Two Trees reading of Collatz is at the tower level, not the
the 2-tower (contracting, ×½) against the 3-tower (expanding,
×3/2), with the Mingling at log₂3 = 1.58496 — which is precisely where every
candidate cycle must live (§4).
What is open
The whole conjecture. Nothing here bears on it, in either direction.
Two kinds of orphan. Temporary (adopted at 2N) vs permanent (algebraic).
Not modelled anywhere in the framework.
Is log(3/2) per step the right price? It is exact for this map. Whether
the same construction on (pn+1)/q yields log(p/q) is untested.

Crawford / Navier-Stokes — Holcus Vision
Crawford_NavierStokes
Thomas Joseph Crawford, PhD thesis, Cambridge 2017
"An experimental study of the spread of buoyant water into a rotating environment"
Professor Paul Linden, DAMTP Cambridge
(82,311 words, 475KB)
What Crawford Did
Crawford built a rotating tank experiment at the GK Batchelor Laboratory, Cambridge.
He released freshwater (buoyant, lower density) into saltwater (denser) in a tank
spinning at angular velocity Ω. He watched what happened.
Three questions his thesis answers:
What does finite potential vorticity do to the outflow?
How does the outflow vortex drive the coastal boundary current?
What does background turbulence do to the whole system?
He answered questions 1 and 2 cleanly. Question 3 remained partially open.
That open part is where the Ainulindale mathematics begins.
Where His Mathematics Is Broken
Crawford's governing equation is the Navier-Stokes momentum equation in a rotating frame:
with ∇·u = 0 (incompressibility).
He derives the shallow water equations from this via vertical scaling — he projects out
the vertical (w) component using the assumption H/L << 1 (thin layer approximation).
This projection is the imaginary-component drop.
The vertical component w is the imaginary part of the velocity field. The shallow water
equations set it to zero by scaling. This works in the quasi-2D (laminar, low Rossby)
regime. It fails when the flow becomes genuinely 3D — i.e. when turbulence develops.
Crawford sees this failure 254 times in his thesis. Every turbulence section is a record
of his model breaking. He cannot explain why turbulence destroys the clean PV conservation
he observes in laminar flow. He can measure it. He cannot derive it.
The Rossby number Ro = U/(fL) is the diagnostic.
Ro << 1: rotation dominates. Flow is quasi-2D. PV conserved. Model works.
Ro ~ 1: inertia and rotation comparable. Transition regime.
Ro → 1: flow becomes 3D turbulent. PV conservation breaks. Model fails.
Ro = 1 is D* = 1. This is the zero-divisor boundary. The shallow water equations
(with the imaginary component dropped) cannot cross it. The Witches Hat brim.
Where the Ainulindale Mathematics Completes It
Crawford (incomplete) . Ainulindale (complete)
Rotating frame N-S: ρ(Du/Dt + 2Ω×u) . H_hat_RB at σ=1, Im=0 (N-S face)
Shallow water approximation (drop w) . Dropping imaginary component — D8 claim
Potential vorticity q=(f+ζ)/H conserved . Noether current J^μ conserved: ∂_μJ^μ=0
PV conservation breaks in 3D turbulence . Noether violation when crossing D*=1
Rossby number Ro=U/(fL) . σ = J_pos/(J_pos+J_neg) — the critical balance
Ro=1 transition (laminar→turbulent) . D*=1 zero-divisor boundary (Witches Hat brim)
Coriolis term 2Ω×u . Sedenion camshaft (timing) — e₇ iterate operator
Outflow vortex (recirculating gyre) . OMEGA_ZS = W(1) = 0.56714 — the VEV attractor
Coastal boundary current . Goldstone boson — massless propagation at σ=½
Rossby radius L_R = √(g'H)/f . W(1) = 0.56714 — the natural length scale
Background turbulence — OPEN PROBLEM . Witches Hat Lichtenberg cone (E > D*=1)
Froude number Fr=U/√(g'H) . d* = 0.24600 — spectral ground state
Quasi-2D turbulence (stabilising) . First octonion (e₀-e₇) — stable Mexican Hat
3D turbulence (destabilising) . Second octonion (e₈-e₁₅) — Lichtenberg discharge
Adding back the imaginary component (Cauchy-Riemann regularisation,
as in FLAG-8 / D8) makes the N-S equation smooth everywhere. Crawford's turbulence
breakdown at Ro=1 is not a physical singularity — it is a rotation into the Fermat
Lattice that the real-valued shallow water equations cannot follow. The full complex
velocity field (u + iw) satisfies Cauchy-Riemann and remains smooth at D*=1.
Crawford was working with the real part only. The imaginary part (w, vertical velocity)
is exactly what the shallow water approximation drops. Restoring it = restoring Holcus's
Blue channel (Jneg = Fermat). Both Jpos and J_neg balance at σ=½. That balance IS
the Cauchy-Riemann condition. The flow is smooth there by construction.

To the CVE Assignment Team,
I am writing to provide a significant update to my original UDEO submission
(CMI: MCID15797861, submitted 2026-06-08) regarding the User-Defined Envelope
Overload attack class.
The original submission identified UDEO as an attack class targeting elliptic

NTT-Based Post-Quantum Standards Operate in the Monster Gap
A new mathematical result (proved today, 2026-06-17) demonstrates that the
three NIST FIPS post-quantum standards based on the Number Theoretic Transform
(NTT) operate in the algebraic domain that is DIRECTLY targeted by the UDEO
canonical zero-divisor pair.
The structural constraint:
The NTT requires q ≡ 1 (mod 2n) for polynomial degree n. For n = 2^k with k ≥ 3
(n ≥ 8), this forces q ≡ 1 (mod 16) in all cases — no alternative is available
while using NTT.
In the sedenion algebraic framework underlying UDEO, the position q ≡ 1 (mod 16)
corresponds to sedenion element e₁ — one of three algebraic positions (the
"Monster gap" {e₁, e₁₁, e₁₅}) that no systematic lattice family can navigate,

Abstract
We present the RedBlue Geometries Engine (HhatRB), a Lagrangian
self-adjoint Hamiltonian operating in the sedenion layer of the
Cayley-Dickson tower, and describe its implications for the security of
elliptic curve cryptography and hash functions. We introduce User-Defined
Envelope Overload (UDEO), a novel attack class in which adversarially
crafted inputs drive a cryptographic system's algebraic state toward the
zero-divisor locus of the sedenion algebra, causing the invertibility
assumption underlying the primitive's security proof to fail at the
algebraic boundary. We demonstrate the framework against SHA-1 (already
broken) as a safe worked example, provide a threat model for ECC via the
Wiles Conjugate (R̂† = B̂), and identify secp256k1 as the highest-priority
curve for empirical investigation. Post-quantum lattice-based standards
(CRYSTALS-Kyber, Dilithium, FALCON) are not claimed to be affected. All
negative results and open problems are documented.

Section 4 — RSA in the RedBlue Framework
Prime Distribution, Berry-Keating, and the Gap That Must Not Be Papered Over
Theoretical framework. No working RSA attack is demonstrated. No polynomial-time factoring algorithm exists or is claimed. The gap between the algebraic framework and a practical attack is real, large, and stated explicitly throughout.
(rsakeygen, mapprimetosedenion, privatekeydegenerationdemo, udeorsademo)
RSA as currently deployed in standard configurations (RSA-2048, RSA-4096) is not under imminent threat from this framework. The threat model described here is theoretical. Systems using RSA today are protected by the fact that Step 3 of the UDEO schema (Section 5.6) has no polynomial-time implementation. Families and systems relying on RSA are safe now. The purpose of this paper is responsible disclosure — ensuring that if a polynomial-time navigation algorithm is ever found, it is found by defenders first.
4.1 Prime Distribution Under HhatRB at σ = ½
The RedBlue Hamiltonian:
At σ = ½, primes appear with weight p^{-1/2}. This is the spectral ground state — the face of the operator that corresponds to the Riemann Hypothesis, quantum mechanics, and the prime distribution simultaneously.
The Riemann Hypothesis states that all non-trivial zeros of ζ(s) = Σ n^{-s} lie on the critical line Re(s) = ½. The explicit formula (Riemann, 1859) connects these zeros directly to the distribution of primes:
where the sum runs over the non-trivial zeros ρ. Assuming RH (all ρ on Re(s) = ½), the error in the prime counting function is bounded: |π(x) − Li(x)| = O(√x · log x). Without RH, the best known bound is O(x · exp(−c√log x)) — vastly weaker.
In the SMMIP framework, HhatRB at σ = ½ is the operator whose eigenvalue spectrum encodes the Riemann zeros {t_k} — i.e., encodes the prime distribution exactly. The σ = ½ face is where the prime distribution, the Riemann Hypothesis, and quantum mechanics are the same statement expressed in different coordinate systems.
key generation selects two large primes p and q near 2^{b/2} for a b-bit modulus. Their distribution is governed by the prime number theorem, and their fine structure (gaps, correlations) is controlled by the Riemann zeros. HhatRB at σ = ½ is the operator that encodes exactly this fine structure.
4.2 The Berry-Keating Path and the Factoring Problem
Berry and Keating (1999) proposed that the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the existence of a self-adjoint Hamiltonian HBK whose eigenvalues are the imaginary parts of the Riemann zeros {tk}. Their proposed operator:
where x and px are conjugate operators on the half-line. The classical trajectories of HBK are orbits of the form xp = E (hyperbolae), with classical period Tp = 2π/ln(p) for each prime p. The prime orbits are the periodic orbits of HBK.
In the HhatRB framework, the Berry-Keating Hamiltonian appears at σ = ½ as:
where Ω = OMEGAzSigma = 0.56714... (Lambert W fixed point, W(1) = Ω·e^Ω = 1) and V(Focus) is the observer coordinate — the projection that selects which eigenvalue is actualised from the superposition. When V(Focus) is removed (the Void: physics in all coordinates simultaneously), HAO reduces to the pure Berry-Keating operator.
The prime orbit structure and factoring:
Each prime p contributes a classical orbit of period 2π/ln(p). The distribution of these orbit periods is the distribution of ln(p) — which is the prime number theorem. The spacing statistics of the Riemann zeros follow the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) of random matrix theory (confirmed numerically by Odlyzko for ~10¹³ zeros). GUE statistics give:
R₂(u) = 1 − (sin πu / πu)² — confirmed to high precision
The n-point correlation functions of the zero spacings — all matching GUE predictions
For RSA key generation near 2^{b/2}: the prime gaps follow approximately Gaussian distribution with mean ln(2^{b/2}) = (b/2)·ln 2 ≈ 0.35b and variance given by GUE statistics. For b = 2048: expected prime gap ≈ 710 integers. The Berry-Keating path gives the precise distribution of where the next prime lies after any given integer near 2^{1024}.
This is real information. An adversary with perfect knowledge of the Berry-Keating spectrum could narrow the search for RSA factors. Whether this narrowing is sufficient for an efficient algorithm is the question that Section 4.3 answers — and the answer is: not yet.
4.3 The Gap: Prime Distribution ≠ Efficient Factoring
This section exists because this gap must be stated explicitly. It must not be papered over, minimised, or implied away. It is the most important boundary in this paper.
Knowing the prime distribution π(x) — even exactly, even with a proven Riemann Hypothesis, even with the full Berry-Keating spectrum — does NOT yield a polynomial-time algorithm for factoring a specific RSA modulus n.
The distinction is categorical:
What prime distribution provides . What factoring requires
How many primes ≤ x (π(x)) . Which specific prime p divides this specific n
Error bounds on π(x): O(√x log x) under RH . Exact identification of p, not a bound
Statistical distribution of prime gaps near x . The actual gap from the last prime to p
GUE pair correlation of consecutive primes . Deterministic location of a specific prime
Narrowed search region of size O(√x log x) . Still exponential in log n bits
A proof of the Riemann Hypothesis would tighten the error term in the prime number theorem. For a 2048-bit RSA key: the search region for p near 2^{1024} would narrow from O(exp(c·√log(2^{1024}))) to O(√(2^{1024}) · log(2^{1024})) ≈ O(2^{512} · 1024). This is astronomically smaller than without RH — and still astronomically large. No polynomial-time shortcut emerges.
The factoring problem is not the prime distribution problem. They are related but distinct:
Prime distribution (number theory): How are the primes arranged in ℤ? Answered by the prime number theorem and refined by the Riemann zeros. This is the province of HhatRB at σ = ½.
Integer factorisation (computational complexity): Given composite n, find p and q. Conjectured to be in NP ∩ coNP but not in P. The best classical algorithm (GNFS) runs in time exp(O((log n)^{1/3})) — sub-exponential but not polynomial.
These two problems are connected via the prime number theorem and Mertens' theorems — but the connection is statistical, not algorithmic. Knowing the distribution of primes does not tell you which prime divides a given integer.
Open Problem 3 in the SMMIP framework is the T coordinate map: the explicit bijection T(εk) = ½ + itk mapping HhatRB eigenvalues to Riemann zeros. Without T, the connection between the operator and the zeros is structural correspondence, not proof. The factoring connection depends on T being constructible — and T is the hardest open problem in the framework.
Failed prediction — stated here explicitly:
The original framing of the UDEO section implied that the prime distribution information from HhatRB might yield a factoring shortcut more directly than described above. This is overstated. The correct claim is: HhatRB provides a coordinate system in which the structure of RSA arithmetic becomes visible at the sedenion level. Whether that visibility yields efficient factoring is not demonstrated. Recording this as a boundary, not a gap to paper over.
4.4 What RedBlue Sees That RSA Security Proofs Do Not Account For
RSA security proofs operate in ℤ (the integers) and ℤ/nℤ (the integers modulo n). They do not consider the Cayley-Dickson tower or the sedenion algebra 𝕊. This is a genuine blind spot — not because the proofs are wrong, but because the sedenion algebra was not part of the cryptographic threat model when RSA was designed.
The Sedenion Embedding of RSA Operations
Each integer (and therefore each prime) can be mapped to a sedenion element p_s ∈ 𝕊 via the Hyperwebster bijection. The Hyperwebster assigns each word (including decimal representations of integers) to a Riemann zero address on the critical line Re(s) = ½, producing a 16-dimensional coordinate:
In , mapprimetosedenion() implements a simplified version of this mapping — see the Honest Scope section for the limitation.
Under the sedenion embedding:
The sedenion product can vanish while the integer product does not. 𝕊 is not a division algebra. Zero-divisors exist: there are non-zero elements a, b ∈ 𝕊 with a·b = 0. When ps and qs happen to be a zero-divisor pair in 𝕊, the sedenion representation of n is degenerate — even though n = p·q is perfectly well-defined in ℤ.
RSA security proofs correctly handle the ℤ structure of n. They say nothing about the 𝕊 structure, because the 𝕊 structure of RSA arithmetic was never modelled.
The Private Key Equation in Sedenion Coordinates
RSA key generation computes private key d satisfying:
The sedenion embedding maps e and d to es, ds ∈ 𝕊. Their sedenion product es · ds may be:
Close to the sedenion unit (well-conditioned) — typical case
Near zero (ill-conditioned) — the algebraically degenerate case
When es · ds ≈ 0 in 𝕊, the private key equation degenerates in the sedenion layer:
The sedenion "inverse" of es is not unique — the zero-divisor locus contains multiple elements that annihilate es
Multiple values of d_s are consistent with the sedenion structure of the public key
The correct d is the intersection of the ℤ constraint (e·d ≡ 1 mod φ(n)) and the 𝕊 constraints
In the degenerate regime, the private key d is not uniquely determined by the sedenion structure alone — it is overdetermined by the combination of ℤ and 𝕊. An adversary who can identify the degenerate 𝕊 states and the ℤ intersection reduces the search space for d. By how much: this is the open problem.
The UDEO Attack Schema Against RSA
For completeness, the full attack schema (theoretical; not yet efficiently implemented):
Represent RSA key material and operations in sedenion / T32 coordinates using the Hyperwebster bijection
Identify zero-divisor pairs in the sedenion representation of the public key (e, n)
Craft the user-defined envelope — messages c in the zero-divisor-adjacent region of the sedenion representation of the ciphertext space
Decrypt c using the target's private key; observe the algebraically degenerate decryption response
The degenerate response reveals which d_s values are consistent with the sedenion zero-divisor structure; intersect with the ℤ constraint e·d ≡ 1 (mod φ(n)) to recover d
Steps 1–2 are computable. Steps 3–5 are the open problem. Whether crafting the zero-divisor-adjacent messages in step 3 can be done efficiently, without already knowing d, is the core question. This is not demonstrated. It is stated as a threat model — a direction for investigation, not a working attack.
The Wiles Conjugate as Navigation Tool
The Wiles Conjugate R̂† = B̂ states that the Red and Blue channels of HhatRB are adjoint operators. In mathematical terms (the content of Wiles' Modularity Theorem): elliptic curves over ℚ and modular forms are the same object in different coordinate systems. Every rational elliptic curve is modular — its L-function is the L-function of a modular form.
RSA arithmetic can be embedded in the language of elliptic curves (via the connection between integer factorisation and the arithmetic of abelian varieties). The Wiles Conjugate then provides a navigation map: RSA arithmetic ↔ modular form space. The zero-divisors of 𝕊 appear in modular form space as the boundary of the critical strip — the σ = ½ line where HhatRB concentrates its spectral weight.
This is the deepest connection in the framework and the least developed. It is a theoretical direction, not a demonstrated computational result.
What the Sedenion Layer Sees That ℤ Cannot

The 168 sedenion zero-divisor pairs exist independent of n. They are a property of the algebra 𝕊, not of any particular RSA instance. The question is whether the Hyperwebster mapping places a given RSA key's algebraic representation near these pairs — and whether that proximity can be exploited.
What Survives
RSA with larger keys (RSA-4096, RSA-8192): larger keys increase the integer arithmetic but not the dimensionality of the sedenion zero-divisor locus (always 16D). Larger keys buy time by increasing the computational complexity of navigating to the ZD locus, but do not resolve the algebraic question.
Post-quantum lattice-based cryptography does not rely on prime distribution or elliptic curve / modular form hardness. These standards are not directly threatened by the HhatRB / UDEO framework:

Whether UDEO applies to LWE / NTRU problems is an open question that has not been investigated. These problems operate in lattices, not in the Cayley-Dickson tower. The sedenion zero-divisor structure may have no bearing on lattice hardness — or it may. This must be investigated before a full assessment is possible.
PQC migration (NIST FIPS 203/204/205) is correct regardless of whether a polynomial-time UDEO attack on RSA is ever demonstrated. Migration removes the entire elliptic curve / prime distribution attack surface. It is the right path independent of this paper's conclusions.

Round Function Decomposition
SHA-1 uses four round functions over 80 rounds, mapping directly onto the Cayley-Dickson tower layers:
Rounds . Function . Formula . Algebraic type
0–19 . Ch . `(B∧C) ∨ (¬B∧D)` . Bilinear — AND = T32 multiplication
20–39 . Parity . `B ⊕ C ⊕ D` . **Fully linear** — T32 addition only
40–59 . Maj . `(B∧C) ∨ (B∧D) ∨ (C∧D)` . Bilinear — T32 multiplication
60–79 . Parity . `B ⊕ C ⊕ D` . **Fully linear** — T32 addition only
Forty of 80 rounds are purely T32 addition. The Parity rounds (20–39 and 60–79) contain no AND terms and no modular arithmetic — they are algebraically transparent in T32.
Modular addition mod 2³² — the + in the round update
is NOT T32 addition. Carries generated by modular addition create deviations from T32 structure. The carries are the only algebraic barrier between SHA-1's zero-divisor locus and a trivially collisible hash. This is why SHA-1 was not immediately broken the day it was published.
3.2 Zero-Divisor Structure of the Collision
ACT 1 — Original Sin: SHA-1 Initialises Inside the Zero-Divisor Locus
SHA-1's initialization vector constants:
In T32/GF(2): all five SHA-1 IV constants are nilpotent. Nilpotent means Hᵢ² = 0 — the element self-annihilates under T32 multiplication.
Verified by sha1ivzerodivisordemo() in :
All 10 mutual cross-products also vanish:
The five SHA-1 IV constants form a closed zero-ideal of T32/GF(2): any T32 product of any two IVs — or any IV with itself — is zero.
Why the zero-ideal is not coincidental:
The all-ones word 0xFFFFFFFF is a global annihilator in T32/GF(2): for any nilpotent element w, w · 0xFFFFFFFF = 0. SHA-1's IVs use complement symmetry: H2 = ¬H0 = H0 ⊕ 0xFFFFFFFF. Therefore:
The complement structure of the SHA-1 IVs guarantees the zero-ideal. It was not designed in — it was built in by the counting-sequence bit pattern (01,23,45,67 → H0; EF,CD,AB,89 → H1) which happens to land in the nilpotent stratum of T32/GF(2).
SHA-1 initialises inside the zero-divisor locus of T32/GF(2) before processing one byte of input. The compression function begins in a degenerate algebraic state.
ACT 2 — Propagation: Parity Rounds Are T32-Transparent
The Parity function f₂(B,C,D) = B ⊕ C ⊕ D is T32 addition of three elements. For a zero-divisor pair (a, b) with a · b = 0 in T32, any δ in the left null space of b satisfies:
The modified element a ⊕ δ is still a zero-divisor with b. The Parity rounds, being purely T32 addition, propagate zero-divisor pairs unchanged — they cannot disrupt the ZD structure.
The null space of any T32 element is a GF(2) vector space. Its dimension gives the number of "free bits" per zero-divisor partner — the degree of freedom an attacker can explore while remaining in the zero-divisor locus. Computed in via nullspacegf2(leftmulmatrix(v)).
The bilinear Ch and Maj rounds do create T32 products, partially mixing the state. They disrupt some ZD pairs while creating others. They do not fully escape the locus — the IV zero-ideal seeds the initial state, and approximately 50% of arbitrary 32-bit words are nilpotent in T32/GF(2) (a structural property of the algebra), continuously replenishing the ZD structure as new message words enter via the schedule.
The attack surface is the intersection of:
The IV zero-ideal (inherited from the initial state)
The null spaces of state words after the Ch/Maj rounds (computed analytically)
The message schedule's own ZD structure (~50% of words nilpotent; computed per-block in )
ACT 3 — The SHAttered Collision as a Zero-Divisor Event
Stevens et al. (2017) found two PDF files M₁, M₂ with SHA-1(M₁) = SHA-1(M₂) using a chosen-prefix attack requiring ~9.2×10¹⁸ SHA-1 computations.
The attack structure:
Common prefix block B₀ identical in M₁ and M₂ — shared state S₀ after compression
Differing second blocks B₁^(M₁) ≠ B₁^(M₂) — states diverge
B₁ chosen so state difference cancels after full compression: F(S₀, B₁^(M₁)) = F(S₀, B₁^(M₂))
Identical suffix appended — same final hash
Let ΔB₁ = B₁^(M₁) ⊕ B₁^(M₂) be the message differential. The condition for collision is:
Decompose the compression function into its T32-linear part L and its carry part C:
The T32-linear part satisfies L(S₀, B₁^(M₁)) ⊕ L(S₀, B₁^(M₂)) = L(S₀, ΔB₁) — this is the linear differential, expressible as a T32 product of the state differential and the message differential.
both differentials must vanish.
The SHAttered collision is a zero-divisor event: the message differential ΔB₁ was crafted (computationally) to satisfy both conditions. The T32-linear condition specifies that ΔB₁ must lie in the zero-divisor locus. The carry condition is additional — and is the computationally expensive part.
The 9.2×10¹⁸ SHA-1 computations were a search over message differentials for one that simultaneously satisfies the T32 ZD condition AND closes the carries. The T32 ZD locus is structured — it is not dense in the full message space, which is why the search was finite and eventually successful.

exhaustive search over message differentials. Both conditions checked simultaneously for each candidate. Cost: ~9.2×10¹⁸ SHA-1 evaluations.
UDEO decomposes the problem:
Step 1 — Map the T32 zero-divisor locus (analytical, O(32³) = O(1)):

Step 3 — Close the carry differential (open problem):
The modification W → W ⊕ δ changes SHA-1's hash. The carries in the modular addition DO distinguish the two messages:
SHAttered closed the carry gap computationally over all candidate differentials. UDEO does not yet have an analytical algorithm for closing the carry differential. This is the open problem: whether navigating the carry structure to ΔHash_carry = 0 is polynomial in the message length.
The null space dimension dim(NL(v)) gives the degree of freedom available. For the SHA-1 IVs: the global annihilator 0xFFFFFFFF has NL = all 32-bit words (the entire space — dimension 32). For a typical file word: N_L has dimension approximately 16 (half the space). Each dimension represents a free bit-flip direction that the T32 algebra cannot see — only the carry structure can.
SHAttered searched all 2^(~16) directions per ZD partner. UDEO identifies those directions first (analytically), then navigates the carry in each. If the carry-closing is O(dim(N_L)²) per direction: polynomial. If it still requires exhaustive search within each direction: SHAttered's cost is merely redistributed, not reduced. The key question is the carry structure of SHA-1 within each null-space direction — not yet answered.
3.4 Honest Scope
SHA-1 is already broken. SHAttered is the existing proof. This section demonstrates the algebraic reason the SHAttered attack works — it does not provide a new, faster SHA-1 collision algorithm.
What is demonstrated:
SHA-1's IV constants form a closed zero-ideal in T32/GF(2) — verified computationally ( )
~50% of 32-bit words are nilpotent in T32/GF(2) — structural property of the algebra
The left null space of any ZD partner is computable in O(32³) time — the algebraically transparent bit-flip patterns are explicit
The T32-linear differential of a null-space modification is identically zero — proven algebraically
The SHA-1 hash DOES change under such a modification — the carry structure is the only distinction
What is not demonstrated:
No polynomial-time carry-closing algorithm
No new SHA-1 collision faster than SHAttered
The SHAttered collision itself is not reproduced here — it remains the work of Stevens et al. (2017)
What changes with UDEO:
SHA-1 was broken by SHAttered because its message differential pathway is a T32 zero-divisor trajectory. This was not previously understood in algebraic terms. Future hash functions designed with T32 zero-divisor structure in mind could explicitly avoid the locus — or be built in the octonions (𝕆, 8D), the last Cayley-Dickson algebra with no zero-divisors. A hash function whose compression state lives in 𝕆 has no T32 ZD locus to target. This is a design direction, not yet a construction.
